Shanghai Municipal Council.

April 24, 1939.

PUBLIC HEALTH DEPARTMENT

Commissioner of Police.

European Refugees.

With reference to letter dated April 17
from the Secretary of the Council, regarding the above,
I have to inform you that Dr. Lucke of this Department
will act as a representative on a Committee to be formed
as suggested in the report of the Special Branch.
At present, Dr. Lucke is absent on short
leave and Mr. Self, a Chief Health Inspector of this
Department will deputise for him.
I shall be obliged if you will kindly inform
me when you propose to have an initial meeting and would
suggest that you ask one of your Staff to arrange direct
with Mr. Self, the time and dates of the future meetings.

Commissioner of Public Health.

CC:MB.

Shanghai, 17th April, 19 39.

The Commissioner of Police:

European Refugees.

The Council has given consideration to
the Special Branch Report of April 4, 1939. The
Council approves the suggestion that a Committee
be formed, as suggested in the Special Branch Report,
and that representatives of the Police Force and
Public Health Department should serve upon it. The
Council further gives authority for the addition of
a representative or representatives of the Public
Works Department should this at any time be found
expedient.

Would you be good enough to take the
necessary initiative in regard to the formation
of this Committee, and arrange direct with the
Commissioner of Public Health as to the appointment
of a representative or representatives from his
Department.

It is important that it should be emphasised
to all concerned that no authority is given to commit
the Council to any financial responsibility, or respon-
sibility for maintenance.

The Council is appreciative of the initiative
that has been shown by the Special Branch in dealing
with this matter.

Subject Central European Jews - Arrival in Shanghai.
Lecture by Mr. Paul KOMOR on April 4, 1939.
Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C Crawford. D. I

During the evening of April 4, 1939 Mr. Paul
KOMOR, one of the responsible committeemen of the
Shanghai Jewish Refugee Relief Societies, gave a
lecture on the refugee problem to some 40 - 50 members
of Toc H at the Holy Trinity Cathedral. The lecture,
which was not open to the press, was sponsored by
Toc H, with the object of permitting its members to
appreciate the problem confronting Shanghai and to
allow them to assist, as they are able, in alleviating
the distress and misery now so prevalent among the
newcomers.

Mr. KOMOR spoke for over an hour and during
this time explained to his audience the manner in
which the committees were caring for the refugees and
how their difficulties were increasing in proportion
with the arrival of further steamers from Europe.
Most of the points he covered have already formed the
subject matter of reports submitted by this office,
but certain aspects of his lecture are given below,
not previously having been recorded in full :

Since relief work commenced in August 1938,
the sum of $343,096.30 local currency has been collected
by the various local organizations, viz :-

American Joint Distribution
Committee, New York -
US.$2,500 and £5,000 - $160,530.00

The Council for German
Jewry (London) £500 - 14,545.00

主题 中欧犹太人 - 抵达上海。
Paul KOMOR 先生于1939年4月4日的演讲。
由 D.S. Pitts 制作，由督察 C Crawford 转呈。

1939年4月4日晚，上海犹太难民救济社负责人之一
Paul KOMOR 先生在圣三一堂向约40至50名“托克H”（Toc H）成员
发表了关于难民问题的演讲。此次演讲不对媒体开放，
由“托克H”主办，旨在让其成员了解上海面临的难题，
并让他们在力所能及的范围内协助缓解新来者中普遍存在的
困苦和悲惨状况。

Up to March 31, 313 persons had been
established in business by means of this fund which,
with families, allowed 660 individuals to become
independent of the Relief Committees.

POSITIONS SECURED
    324 persons have now secured jobs in Shanghai,
thus making 420 persons independent of the Relief
Committees.
    In addition to these figures, 488 German
Jewish families of which at least one member of
each has been incarcerated in a concentration camp,
have arrived in Shanghai with funds placed at their
disposal by the "HICEM" Relief Society, Paris.
    In all US.$24,058.00 and £232 have been
handed to these families, figures which are
equivalent to $175,000.00. The families concerned
are compelled to live on the amounts given them by
the Paris Society and receive no help in Shanghai.

CAMPS
(1)    The Foreign Women's Home, Whashing Road,
       has been taken over and is being utilized as
       a hospital, it being too costly for cases to
       be sent to the General or Country Hospitals.
(2)    Premises at 138 Ward Road and 150 Wayside
       Road, have been repaired and made habitable.
       Kitchens have been installed and close on
       1400 can be accommodated.

Date April 4, 1939.
Subject Central European Jews - Arrival in Shanghai
Made by D. S. Pitte Forwarded by C. Crawford S.I.

In regard to the second paragraph of the
communication dated March 28 addressed to the
Commissioner of Police from the Secretary, I have
to report that I have interviewed Mr. M. SPEELMAN, who
is at the head of the Jewish Refugee Committees and
organizations now functioning in Shanghai.
The salient points of the reports submitted on
March 15 and March 21 headed "Central European Jews -
Arrival in Shanghai," were carefully brought to Mr.
SPEELMAN's attention, after which he was informed of
the urgent necessity and advisability of placing the
entire refugee question and its attendant problems under
the control of a board or committee approved by the
Municipal Council, which would work in co-operation with
the organizations now existing for the care of the
newcomers.
The points as particularly affecting this Police
Force as outlined in the report of March 21 were then
explained to Mr. SPEELMAN together with the obvious
reasons for the need of their enforcement.
Mr. KOMOR, Chairman of the "I.C." Committee,
190 Kiukiang Road, was in Mr. SPEELMAN's office during
the interview and he fully endorsed everything that was
said with the result that Mr. SPEELMAN expressed his
unqualified approval of the whole scheme which he
realises will have the affect of greatly improving
the status of the present Committees in the eyes of

关于秘书于3月28日致警务处处长的公函第二段，本人谨报告称，我已会见 M. SPEELMAN 先生，他是目前在上海运作的犹太难民委员会及组织的负责人。
3月15日和3月21日提交的题为“中欧犹太人 - 抵达上海”的报告中的要点已仔细提请 SPEELMAN 先生注意，随后告知他，迫切需要将整个难民问题及其相关问题置于一个经工部局批准的董事会或委员会的控制之下，并与现有照顾新来者的组织合作开展工作，此举具有必要性和可取性。
接着向 SPEELMAN 先生解释了3月21日报告中概述的特别影响本警队的要点，以及执行这些措施的显而易见的原因。
在会谈期间，“I.C.”委员会主席 KOMOR 先生（九江路190号）也在 SPEELMAN 先生的办公室，他完全赞同所说的一切，结果是 SPEELMAN 先生表示对整个方案无条件批准，他意识到这将大大改善现有委员会在

both refugee and non-refugee circles, will permit
proper control to be exercised over recalcitrant
members and/or bad characters of the Jewish refugees
and will allow the Council's various departments to
assist in officially combatting the menaces of a
problem that at the moment is nearly impossible of

    Mr. SPEELMAN expressed his pleasure at the
fact that the Council had interested itself through
the Police in the problem and promised to give every
assistance and aid that he was able to in co-operating
with the Council or Police in any proposed schemes.

    He also indicated that there was no necessity
to approach other local influential Jews of long
residence who were doing all they could to alleviate
the plight of their more unfortunate brethren, as he
felt quite certain that the scheme would also receive
their fullest approval.

    Mr. SPEELMAN was asked to note that the
Council's proposed action was not to be interpreted
to mean that any responsibility for the maintenance
of refugees would be assumed. Mr. SPEELMAN
acknowledged this fact but remarked that he intended
applying to the Council for a remission of rates on
buildings now serving as shelters and camps for the
refugees.

    SPEELMAN 先生对工部局通过警方关注这一问题表示高兴，并承诺在任何拟议的方案中与工部局或警方合作，提供他所能给予的一切协助和支持。

    他还指出，没有必要去接触其他长期居住在当地、正竭尽全力缓解其更不幸同胞困境的有影响力犹太人，因为他确信该方案也会得到他们的充分认可。

    已请 SPEELMAN 先生注意，工部局拟采取的行动不应被解释为意味着将承担维持难民生计的任何责任。SPEELMAN 先生承认这一事实，但 remarked 称他打算向工部局申请减免目前用作难民收容所和营地的建筑物的捐税。

    Mr. SPEELMAN is leaving Shanghai for New York,
Washington, London, Paris and Berlin before the end of
the current month in an effort to secure financial
support for the refugees in Shanghai. His position
will be taken over by Mr. Ellis HAYIM upon his
departure. In the meanwhile Mr. SPEELMAN will be
pleased to receive any communications and/or visitors
from the Council to discuss the formation of the
proposed committee or board with the object of having
it placed in operation as soon as possible.
    It is of great significance to note that the
total number of arrivals now exceeds 6,000, an
increase of nearly 2,000 in the past 2½ weeks.
    It is respectfully suggested that Mr. SPEELMAN
and/or Mr. Ellis HAYIM and Mr. KOMOR be included as
members of any board that the Council approves, for
these gentlemen have been dealing with the refugee
problem for many months and will be naturally in a
position to render able assistance to other members
on questions that require clarification and
explanation.

ADMINISTRATION BUILDING.

Shanghai, 28th March, 1939.

The Commissioner of Police:

European Refugees.

Your report of March 23, together with
attached reports, has received the consideration
of the Council.

The Council desires that you initiate dis-
cussions with responsible members of the Committees
referred to on the lines that you suggest. Before
any scheme is finally agreed upon, it should be
submitted to the Council for consideration.

In commenting upon the circular which I sent
round to the Council, the Vice-Chairman remarks that
the Council must not take any action which can possibly
be interpreted to mean that it is, or ever will be, in
any way responsible for the maintenance of the refugees
in question.

Another Member remarks that he thinks that the
Police might initiate discussions at once, but he does
not understand how refugees can be compelled to record
particulars, etc. He adds: "Moreover, if all particulars

characters will be reliable?"

Special Branch,
March 23, 1939.

Commissioner.
Sir,

Central European Jews - Arrival in Shanghai.

Reference attached report by D.S. Pitts, whatever
action the Council proposes taking will have to be taken
with all possible haste as with constant arrivals by
German and Italian ships the present number will increase
by leaps and bounds. Since D.S. Pitts gave an estimate
of 4,000, there have been some 800 fresh arrivals and
there is every reason to anticipate that present develop-
ments in Europe will result in arrivals in even greater
numbers just as fast as the shipping companies can cope
with them. It must be realized that Shanghai is the only
port in the world where these unfortunates can enter
freely and that by the end of the year the number may
quite possibly exceed that of the Russian invasion following
Soviet assumption to power. Again, these people differ
from the Russian emigrants as a big percentage of them
are persons of culture and the brains of industry in the
place from which they were ousted.

The question is of such magnitude that to secure
supervision over these people to any effective degree
it will be necessary to bring into discussions or invite
opinion from responsible members of the present committees,
one or more of the prominent members of the Jewish community
who are interesting themselves financially in the matter
and perhaps several of the leading refugees themselves.
The scheme put forward by D.S. Pitts seems feasible but
discussions on the lines indicated are, I think, absolutely
essential to a successful solution.

J.W. Pollock
D.C. (Special Branch)

特科，
1939年3月23日。

致警务处长。
先生，

中欧犹太人——抵达上海。

参照附件中 D.S. Pitts 的报告，无论工部局拟采取何种行动，均需尽快实施，因为随着德国和意大利船只的不断抵达，现有难民人数将急剧增加。自 D.S. Pitts 估算4,000人以来，又有约800名新抵者，且有充分理由预期，鉴于欧洲目前的局势，只要航运公司运力允许，抵达人数将以更快的速度进一步大幅增加。必须认识到，上海是世界上这些不幸之人能够自由入境的唯一港口，到年底时，其人数完全有可能超过苏维埃掌权后俄国入侵（指俄国内战及革命后难民潮）时期的人数。此外，这些人与俄国移民不同，他们中很大比例是有文化的人，也是被驱逐地工业界的精英。

此事规模如此之大，若要对此类人群进行有效监管，有必要让目前各委员会中负责任的成员参与讨论或征求意见，其中包括一两位在财务上关注此事的犹太社区知名人士，或许还包括几位主要的难民代表。D.S. Pitts 提出的方案看似可行，但我认为，按照上述思路进行讨论对于成功解决此问题绝对必要。

J.W. Pollock
副督察长（特科）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No..........
Section 1, Special br. Sidutch,
REPORT    Date March 21, 19 39.
Subject Central European Jews - Arrival in Shanghai.
Made by D. S. Pitts    Forwarded by C. Gouska. D. J.

With reference to the contents of the second
paragraph of the communication dated March 20 from
the Secretary of the Shanghai Municipal Council
addressed to the Commissioner of Police, the follow-
ing are brief details of a scheme, which if put into
effect, would permit the competent authorities to
control the movements of the newly-arrived Central
European Jews to a far greater degree than now
possible.

As outlined in the report of March 15, the number
of refugees arriving here is assuming such vast
proportions that the Committees now caring for them
may, and probably will, find themselves in a position
before long where they cannot exercise full responsibility
for the comings and goings of those Jews registering
with them.

It is respectfully suggested that the entire
problem be placed under the control of a board or
committee sponsored by the Municipal Council with one
or more members of the Special and/or Crime Branches
of Police Headquarters co-opted thereon, this board
or committee to act in concert with the present
existing relief organizations.

It should be made compulsory for each and every
refugee arriving in Shanghai to record with the new
Committee his name, details as to his passport, past
activities, address in Shanghai, profession and all
other particulars required. All changes in residence
in Shanghai must be brought to the notice of the new

正如3月15日报告中所述，抵达此地的难民数量已达到如此巨大的规模，以至于目前负责照顾他们的各委员会可能、而且很可能不久就会发现自身处于无法对向其登记的犹太人的来去行使完全责任的境地。

谨建议将整个问题置于由工部局赞助的一个董事会或委员会的控制之下，并从警察总局特科和/或刑案科抽调一名或多名成员加入该董事会或委员会，该机构应与现有的救济组织协同行动。

应强制要求每一位抵达上海的难民向新委员会登记其姓名、护照详情、过往活动、在上海的住址、职业以及所有其他所需 particulars。在上海住所的任何变更都必须通知新

    Further, information secured since submitting
the last report, indicates that in the midst of the
refugees now concentrated in Shanghai are quite a
number of individuals who are definitely regarded as
bad characters. A few have shown their qualities
already and it can be assumed that if any criminals
have arrived with the newcomers, it is only a question
of time before their activities are manifested.
    If this does happen to any large degree and no
control is exercised over the movements of these
people, then the Police can confidently look forward
to a crime wave. Certain elements among the

dissatisfaction with the existing Committees solely

ADMINISTRATION BUILDING

Shanghai, 20th March, 1939.

The Commissioner of Police:

European Refugees.

May I refer to the interesting Police Report
of March 18.

Would you please amplify your views on the
question of "measures put into effect in order to control
the movements of all Jewish arrivals".

It is stated that there is attached a report on
the work of the I.C. Committee and also a list of profes-
sions of registered refugees as compiled by the Committee
of Dr. Marx. The list of professions does not, in fact,
appear to be attached. I would be interested to have a
copy.

Secretary.

S. 1, Special Branch,
REPORT.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE File No. ... Y No D 5422 (c) Branch ... 7-39 Date March 15, 1939）

Subject Central European Jews - Arrival in Shanghai

Made by D. S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Crawford S J

With almost every steamer from Europe
bringing more and more Jewish refugees to Shanghai,
the total number of arrivals now is well in excess
of 4,000. These unfortunate people are leaving
the Central European countries in ever increasing
numbers and it is learned that every available
German and Italian ship is fully booked up until
the end of June, 1939, by which time the number of
refugees in Shanghai will probably amount to 8,000
or more.

As things stand at present two committees
work in co-operation in caring for these Jews.
These are the :-

(1) Relief Society for German and Austrian Jews,
1 South Tiendong Road with Dr. MARX in
charge, and

(2) "I.C." (International Committee),
190 Kiukiang Road, with Mr. P. KUMOR
in charge.

Both organizations are doing excellent work
on funds that are always dwindling, but the
impression is gained that the numerically small
staffs are now being faced with innumerable
difficulties.

With but a handful of persons, not previously
accustomed to work of the nature that they must now
undertake, virtually controlling the destinies of
two-thirds of the refugees already in Shanghai, it

上海公共租界工部局警务处。

报告。
（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 档案号 ... Y 号 D 5422 (c) 分部 ... 7-39 日期 1939年3月15日）

主题 中欧犹太人——抵达上海

撰写人 D. S. Pitts 转呈人 C. Crawford S J

随着几乎每一艘从欧洲驶来的轮船都将越来越多的犹太难民带到上海，目前的抵达总数已远远超过4,000人。这些不幸的人正以日益增长的数量离开中欧各国，据悉，所有可用的德国和意大利船只直至1939年6月底均已订满，届时上海的难民人数可能达到8,000人或更多。

就目前情况而言，有两个委员会合作照顾这些犹太人。它们是：

(1) 德奥犹太难民救济协会，
地址：天潼路南1号，负责人：MARX（马克思）博士，以及

(2) “I.C.”（国际委员会），
地址：九江路190号，负责人：P. KUMOR（库莫尔）先生。

这两个组织在资金不断减少的情况下开展了卓越的工作，但给人的印象是，人数不多的工作人员现在正面临无数的困难。

仅仅依靠少数几个人，他们此前并不习惯于从事现在必须承担的性质的工作，却实际上掌控着已在上海的三分之二难民的命运，这

is not difficult to envisage the responsibility that
falls on their shoulders. For instance, never less
than 200 - often very many more - immigrants are to
be seen daily in the offices of the "I.C." at 190
Kiukiang Road. Their needs are many and each and
every one has to be personally interviewed by members
of the staff in order that their (the immigrants')
wants and requirements can be adequately and justly
considered. The needs of these poor unfortunates are
many, as mentioned above, and range from cultured
women with infants at their breasts tearfully begging
for a few dollars for their children, to diplomæd
professional men and women endeavouring to secure
loans with which to commence business once again.

The Committees conduct their work in a manner
that is most praiseworthy and on the whole are
handling the situation fairly satisfactorily. But,
and this is of prime importance, when the number of
immigrants doubles the present total - and it will
not be very long before such developments are a
matter of fact - these committees are most assuredly
going to find their hands more than full. Even now,
despite the fact that refugees already here are being
taken care of in a way that is commensurate with the
finances at the disposal of the Committees, many of
these Jews have reached the end of their resources
and will turn their hands to anything in desperation.

不难想象落在他们肩上的责任。例如，每天在九江路190号的“国际委员会”办公室里，至少可以看到200名——通常远多于此——移民。他们的需求多种多样，每一位都必须由工作人员亲自面谈，以便充分且公正地考虑他们（移民们）的愿望和要求。如上所述，这些可怜的不幸者的需求繁多，从怀抱婴儿、泪流满面地为孩子乞求几美元的知识女性，到试图获得贷款以重新创业的专业持证男女人士，不一而足。

各委员会以值得高度赞扬的方式开展其工作，总体而言，对局势的处理相当令人满意。但是，这一点至关重要，当移民人数达到目前总数的两倍时——这种情况不久就会成为事实——这些委员会肯定会感到应接不暇。即便现在，尽管已在此地的难民得到的照顾与各委员会可支配的资金相称，但许多犹太人已经耗尽了资源，将在绝望中不惜做任何事情。

FM. 2
G. SOM-F-39

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............

REPORT                      Station,
- 3 -                       Date....................19

Subject....................................................................................................

Made by....................................................Forwarded by............................................................

Rumours which persist in going the rounds tend to
indicate that the greater percentage of those persons
who have arrived are well off financially. While it
is perfectly true that some of them have money of
their own - details are given later in this report -
careful investigation shows conclusively that in the
main, most of them are with nothing more than their
clothes and what they are supplied in the way of food
and lodgings and/or a dole by either of the Committees.

The people suffering most in this situation
are those of the cultured and professional classes,
many of whom, in their previous lives in Austria and
Germany, were highly respected citizens. They are
unable to secure positions in Shanghai and forced to
live under conditions that, prior to the journey to
the Far East, they had never even given a thought.
For instance, among the Jews now existing in one of
the Refugee Camps in the Wayside district is a
Dr. Gabriel LAX, a Police Commissioner of Vienna
prior to the advent of the Nazis. Dr. LAX is spoken
of as being a brilliant criminologist recognised as
a leading man in his profession by European Police
Forces. As an inmate of the Camp, he receives a bed
and food and nothing else. He has no job and thus
his mental attainments are being blunted day by day.
It is, therefore, not difficult to envisage how this
particular individual regards his stay in Shanghai and
his case is definitely typical of many hundred others.

制作人....................................................转呈人............................................................

持续流传的谣言倾向于表明，抵达者中大部分人在经济上较为宽裕。虽然确实有些人拥有自己的资金——本报告后文将提供细节——但仔细调查确凿地显示，总体而言，他们大多数人除了身上的衣物以及由任一委员会提供的食物、住宿和/或救济金外，身无长物。

在此境况下受苦最深的是受过教育和从事专业阶层的人士，其中许多人在此前于奥地利和德国的生活中曾是备受尊敬的公民。他们无法在上海谋得职位，被迫生活在一种在前往远东之前甚至从未设想过的条件下。例如，目前在兆丰路（Wayside district）地区的一个难民营中居住的犹太人中，有一位加布里埃尔·拉克斯（Gabriel LAX）博士，他在纳粹上台前曾任维也纳警察局长。拉克斯博士被誉为一位杰出的犯罪学家，被欧洲警察部队公认为其行业内的领军人物。作为难民营的一名收容人员，他仅获得一张床位和食物，别无其他。他没有工作，因此他的心智才能正日益钝化。因此，不难想象这位特定人士如何看待他在上海的逗留，而他的情况绝对代表了其他数百人的典型状况。

Three professional men have already committed
suicide, being unable to put up with conditions as
they find them here.

All this leads up to another very important
point - a point that affects this Police Force.
In every very large body of men and women there is
invariably a certain number of bad characters.
When persons do not get enough to eat and drink,
when people are on the verge of desperation, certain
of them are unable to resist temptation and the
result is crime. When such a statement is made
there is no reason to infer that crime will manifest
itself in any large degree among the newcomers, but
with the number of refugees always growing and the
amount of money with which to care for them becoming
proportionately less, jobs becoming scarcer and the
possibilities of opening businesses decreasing week
by week, such a development cannot be overlooked.
In fact the potential factors for an increase in
crime are already established and with this in mind
it follows that action by the Shanghai Municipal
Council would seem imperative and some measures put
into effect in order to control the movements of all
Jewish arrivals. Already two concrete instances
have come to the notice of this office in regard to
the attempts by young German Jews to secure money
by fraudulent means.

所有这一切引出了另一个非常重要的问题——一个影响本警察部队的问题。在任何庞大的男女群体中， invariably 总有一定数量的不良分子。当人们吃不饱喝不足时，当人们处于绝望边缘时，其中某些人无法抵抗诱惑，结果便是犯罪。做出这样的陈述并非暗示犯罪将在新来者中大范围显现，但随着难民人数不断增加，用于照顾他们的资金相应减少，工作机会日益稀缺，开设生意的可能性逐周降低，这种发展趋势不容忽视。事实上，导致犯罪增加的潜在因素已经形成，鉴于此，上海工部局采取行动似乎是势在必行的，并应实施某些措施以控制所有犹太抵达者的行动。本办事处已注意到两起具体案例，涉及年轻的德国犹太人试图通过欺诈手段获取钱财。

As matters stand at present, we are dependent
on the Refugee Committees for information relating to
the activities and comings and goings of the immigrants.
It is not suggested that these Committees are
unwilling to cooperate with the Police but the time
is not far away when the staff members of such
committees will have so much to attend to that they
will have insufficient time to attend to details
that are most important to this Force.

From conversations held with various new
arrivals it is learned that the general opinion of
the refugees is divided in regard to further batches
being allowed to come to Shanghai. It is realised
that with each addition to the already existing
number, the chances for those here to secure positions
will be decreased but, on the other hand, Shanghai is
at present the only place in the world which refugee
Jews may enter without question.

If no measures are taken by the competent
authorities to prevent a further influx, Shanghai
can expect to have at least 12,000 German and
Austrian Jews in its portals before the end of the
current year. Should this happen there is little
doubt that a problem, analogous in all respects to
that of the trek from Russia to Shanghai of the
White Russians after the Revolution, will present
itself. Further comment is unnecessary.

就目前情况而言，我们依赖难民委员会提供有关移民活动及往来的信息。并非暗示这些委员会不愿与警方合作，但为时不远，此类委员会的工作人员将有太多事务需要处理，以至于没有足够的时间来处理对本部队最为重要的细节。

通过与各种新抵达者的交谈得知，难民们对于是否允许更多批次的人员来到上海的意见存在分歧。人们意识到，随着现有数量的每一次增加，此处人员谋得职位的机会将会减少，但另一方面，上海目前是世界上难民犹太人无需质疑即可进入的唯一地方。

如果主管当局不采取措施防止进一步涌入，上海可以预期在今年年底前至少有12,000名德国和奥地利犹太人抵达其门户。如果发生这种情况，毫无疑问，将出现一个在各方面都类似于革命后白俄从俄罗斯迁徙至上海的问题。无需 further comment。

Arrangements have already been made by the
responsible Committees to take over the London
Mission Compound in Chaoufoong Road, which when
renovated, will serve as another camp to house
new arrivals.

Despite the fact that a the proportion of the
newcomers are securing positions, the Jews are placed
in a very awkward position. Mr. KOMOR, by virtue of
the office he holds, will not permit the immigrants
to hold posts that will have the effect of displacing
other foreigners from employment. A few instances have
already come to light where qualified refugees have
had the opportunity of securing jobs at rates greatly
below the wages offered other foreigners. Mr. KOMOR,
however, will not permit such positions to be taken
up although he realises full well that sooner or later
certain circles in Shanghai will say that either the
refugees have no desire to work or they will oust
other foreigners by working at cut rates:

Facilities for the education of children of
school age are well cared for by the Committees, but
the drain on the finances is becoming heavier with
each month..

page_data.en:
REPORT OF THE "INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE"
Up to February 28, 1939.

The "International Committee" commenced its
activities in August 1938 in the support of European
refugees. During the first few months, the whole work
was performed and carried out by Mr. Komor in his
private office. Later an assistant placed himself at
Mr. Komor's disposal without remuneration. As the
number of refugees increased, so the work proportionally
expanded; and consequently the number of assistants
have been gradually increased so that they now total
ten persons. As already mentioned, the work of the
"International Committee" was carried out until December
1938 in the private office of Mr. Komor, no
administrative expenses having been incurred and early
in 1939 was transferred to its present address. The
total administrative expenses for office supplies,
postage, travelling expenses, light, telephones etc.,
now amount to the sum of C$800.66.

The business of the "International Committee"
consisted not only of the simple provisioning of
emigrants, which was carried out systematically, even
if it required a great deal of time, as each case had
to be dealt with individually, but one had always to
take into consideration that the entire question was
one of dealing with persons driven from their homes
and deprived of all means of subsistence and who, in
their desperation, had reached the end of their
resources. It was attempted, through personal contact
to explain to these people that the available means
were limited but notwithstanding these circumstances
page_data.zh:
“国际委员会”报告
截至1939年2月28日。

“国际委员会”于1938年8月开始开展援助欧洲难民的活动。在最初的几个月里，所有工作均由科莫尔（Komor）先生在其私人办公室内完成和执行。后来，一名助手无偿听候科莫尔先生调遣。随着难美人数的增加，工作量也相应扩大；因此，助手的人数逐渐增加，目前总数已达十人。如前所述，“国际委员会”的工作直至1938年12月一直在科莫尔先生的私人办公室进行，未产生任何行政费用，并于1939年初迁至现址。目前，办公用品、邮资、差旅费、水电费、电话费等行政费用总计为法币800.66元。

“国际委员会”的业务不仅包括系统地为难民提供生活物资——尽管这需要大量时间，因为每个案例都必须单独处理——而且必须始终考虑到，整个问题的核心是应对那些被赶出家园、剥夺了一切生计手段、并在绝望中耗尽资源的人群。委员会试图通过个人接触向这些人解释，可用资源是有限的，但尽管如此

page_data.en:
- 2 -

every possible endeavour would be made to come to their
assistance with advice and still better with material
aid.

Numerous recommendations, attempts to obtain
"employment, personal and written requests were
required to be made in order to find positions for
at least a small portion of the huge number of refugees.
By November 1938, the "International Committee" had
undertaken all negotiations on behalf of the refugees
with the authorities, especially with the German
Consulate-General. Since then over 2,000 passes
have been registered through the "International
Committee" at the German Consulate-General and over
1,000 Identification Cards have been issued. It also
registered roughly 1,200 changes of Christian surnames, and
dealt with over 300 documents which required official
attestation.

During these period approximately 200 persons
appeared before the "International Committee" daily
partly with requests for aid and partly in connection
with other matters which were dealt with in private
and above all to their satisfaction. From the
Committee's inception two persons were removed from
its offices for improper conduct.

Its further activities included the receiving
of petitions for loans and all administrative
operations connected therewith. In particular it
consulted all petitioners for loans and after approval
took care of the disbursement and control of paid out
sums. Special difficulties were encountered in the
way of settling differences between partners who
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

仍将尽一切可能通过建议，尤其是通过物质援助来帮助他们。

为了至少为一小部分数量庞大的难民找到职位，需要进行大量的推荐、尝试获取“就业机会”、以及提出个人和书面请求。截至1938年11月，“国际委员会”已代表难民与当局，特别是与德国总领事馆进行了所有谈判。自那时以来，已有超过2,000份通行证通过“国际委员会”在德国总领事馆登记，并签发了超过1,000张身份证。此外，还登记了大约1,200次基督教姓氏的变更，并处理了超过300份需要官方认证的文件。

在此期间，每天约有200人来到“国际委员会”，部分是为了寻求援助，部分是为了处理其他事项，这些事项均在私下处理，且主要令当事人满意。自委员会成立之初，有两人因行为不当被请离办公室。

其后续活动还包括接收贷款申请以及与之相关的所有行政操作。特别是，委员会咨询了所有贷款申请人，并在批准后负责发放款项及监控已支付金额的使用情况。在解决合伙人之间的分歧方面遇到了特殊困难，这些合伙人

page_data.en:
- 3 -

became acquainted with each other just before the
establishment of businesses and soon afterwards
developed differences of opinion, and in finding
suitable solutions for the continuance of their
enterprises.

Out of the capital of C$15,700, which was
originally placed at the Committee's disposal and
the rehabilitation fund of C$150,000 which was
subsequently created thanks to the high minded gift
of Sir Victor Sasson, 218 applicants for loans (with
total family membership of about 420 persons), who
are partly registered with the "International Committee",
partly with the Marx Committee, received money to the
total of C$95,000 for the purpose of creating new
existences and to make themselves independent. Enclosed
is a list, classified according to branches of business
enterprises.

A further 157 persons, (which number by inclusion
of family members increases to 206) have secured
positions and are excluded from further assistance.
This number refers, however, only to persons registered
with the "International Committee".

The provisioning itself included the disbursement
of rent and food allowances, the distribution of meal
tickets, the establishment of various eating stations,
and of assignments for medical attention and medicines,
accomodation of children in schools, when it was
impossible for them to attend the Jewish School,
accomodation of children among local families
approached through advertisements in the press, and
the working up of special cases, which often required
several days.

Rechenschaftsbericht des "I.C." per 28.2.1939.
--------------------------------------------------

Das "I.C." nahm seine Taetigkeit im August 1938 auf und befasste
sich mit der Unterstuetzung europaeischer Fluechtlinge. Die gesamte
Arbeit wurde in den ersten Monaten von Herrn Komor allein und zwar
in seinem Privat-Office geleistet. Spaeter stellte sich eine Hilfs-
kraft freiwillig ohne jegliches Entgelt zur Verfuegung. Mit der
gewaltigen Zunahme der Fluechtlinge und der damit verbundenen Mehr-
arbeit wurde die Anzahl der Hilfskraefte allmaehlich vermehrt und
betraegt heute durchschnittlich 10 Personen. Das "I.C.", welches
wie erwaehnt bis Dezember 1938 im Privat-Office des Herrn Komor be-
stand und keinerlei Regiekosten verursachte, wurde im Jahre 1939
in die jetzigen Raeume verlegt. Die gesamten Verwaltungskosten
fuer Bureau-Artikel, Porti, Fahrgelder, Licht, Telefon etc. betra-
gen bis zum heutigen Tage Sh.$800.66.

Die Agenden des "I.C." umfassten schliesslich nicht nur die reine
Fuersorge, welche zwar systematisch durchgefuehrt werden konnte,
dennoch enorm viel Zeit in Anspruch nahm, weil nach Moeglichkeit
jeder Fall individuell behandelt werden sollte. Man musste immer
darauf Ruecksicht nehmen, dass es sich um verjagte, sicherlich auch
aller Mittel entbloesste Menschen handelt, welche in ihrer Verzweif-
lung keinen Ausweg mehr finden konnten. Es wurde versucht, diesen
Menschen in persoenlicher Aussprache die Beschraenktheit der Mittel
klarzulegen und ihnen trotzdem im Rahmen der Moeglichkeit mit Rat
und vor allem mit Tat beiseite zu stehen. Unzaehlige Befuerwortungs-
schreiben, Stellenvermittlungs-Versuche, persoenliche und schrift-
liche Interventionen waren notwendig, um wenigstens einen kleinen
Teil aus der grossen Anzahl von Fluechtlingen unterzubringen.

Schon im November 1938 uebernahm es das "I.C.", fuer alle Fluecht-
linge mit den Behoerden, vor allem mit dem Deutschen Generalkonsu-
lat, als Verbindungsglied zu verhandeln. Es wurden seit diesem
Zeitpunkt ueber 2000 Paesse durch das "I.C." beim Deutschen General-
konsulat registriert, ueber 1000 Legitimationen des "I.C." ausgege-
page_data.zh:
“国际委员会”（I.C.）截至1939年2月28日的责任报告。
--------------------------------------------------

“国际委员会”于1938年8月开始运作，致力于援助欧洲难民。最初几个月的工作完全由科莫尔（Komor）先生在其私人办公室独自承担。后来，一名助手自愿无偿提供服务。随着难民人数的激增以及随之而来的工作量增加，助手的人数逐渐增多，目前平均为10人。“国际委员会”如前所述，在1938年12月之前一直设在科莫尔先生的私人办公室，未产生任何管理费用，于1939年迁至现址。截至目前，办公用品、邮资、车费、照明、电话等全部行政费用共计上海银元800.66元。

“国际委员会”的事务最终不仅包括纯粹的福利救济工作——这项工作虽然可以系统地进行，但由于尽可能对每个案例进行个别处理，因此耗费了大量时间。人们必须始终考虑到，这些人是被驱逐的，肯定也剥夺了所有手段，在绝望中找不到出路。我们试图通过个人谈话向这些人阐明资源的局限性，并在可能的范围内为他们提供建议，尤其是实际行动上的支持。为了至少安置大批难民中的一小部分，无数封推荐信、职业介绍尝试、个人和书面干预都是必要的。

早在1938年11月，“国际委员会”就承担起作为所有难民与当局（特别是德国总领事馆）之间联络纽带进行谈判的职责。自那时起，“国际委员会”已在德国总领事馆登记了2000多本护照，签发了1000多份“国际委员会”身份证明，

page_data.en:
-2-
ben, in ungefaehr 1200 Faellen die Vornamens-Aenderung angemeldet
und mehr als 300 Schriftstuecke, welche amtlich beglaubigt werden
mussten, erledigt.
In der gleichen Zeit wurden taeglich ca 200 Parteien, welche teils
wegen Fuersorge, teils in anderen Angelegenheiten beim "I.C." er-
schienen, in Ruhe und vor allem zu deren Befriedigung abgefertigt;
Waehrend der ganzen Taetigkeit des "I.C." mussten nur 2 Personen,
welche sich aeusserst ungebuehrlich benahmen, durch Ordner aus
dem Office entfernt werden.
Zu den weiteren Agenden gehoertedie administrative Bearbeitung
der eingebrachten Darlehnsgesuche, vor allem aber auch die Beratung
der Darlehns-Bewerber, und nach Bewilligung die Auszahlung und Kon-
trolle der ausgezahlten Gelder. - Besondere Muehe verursachte es,
Differenzen zwischen Partnern, welche sich erst kurz vor der Ge-
schaef tsgruendung kennen lernten und bald nach der Geschaeftsgruen-
dung in Meinungsverschiedenheiten gerieten, zu bereinigen, und fuer
den Weiterbestand dieser Unternehmungen geeignete Loesungen zu fin-
den.
Aus dem urspruenglich zur Verfuegung gestellten Kapital von
Sh.$15,700.-- und dem nachtraeglich dank der hochherzigen Spende
des Sir Victor Sassoon gegruendeten Rehabilitation-Fund ($150,000.-)
konnten bisher 218 Darlehns-Bewerber (mit Familien-Anhang ca 420
Personen) welche teils beim "I.C.", teils beim Committee Marx regi-
striert sind, Darlehn zur Existenzgruendung im Gesamtbetrage von
ca Sh.$95,000,-- erhalten und sich selbstaendig machen. Im Anhang
ist eine nach Branchen geordnete Liste beigefuegt.
Weiters konnten 157 Personen, welche mit Familienangehoerigen sich
auf 206 erhoebt, in Stellungen unterkommen und aus der Fuersorge
gestrichen werden. Diese Zahlen betreffen jedoch nur die beim "I.C."
registrierten Personen.
Die Fuersorge selbst umfasste die Auszahlung von Wohnungs- und
Nahrungszuschuessen, die Ausgabe von Esstickets seit Errichtung
der diversen Speisestellen, Aerzte- und Medikamenten-Zuweisung,
Unterbringung
page_data.zh:
-2-
在约1200个案例中申报了名字变更，并处理了300多份需要官方认证的文件。
在同一时期，每天约有200名当事人因福利救济或其他事务来到“国际委员会”，均得到平静且主要令其满意的接待；在“国际委员会”整个运作期间，只有2名行为极不检点的人被管理员请出办公室。
其他事务还包括对提交的贷款申请进行行政处理，特别是为贷款申请人提供咨询，以及在批准后发放贷款并监控已发放的资金。特别费力的是调解那些在创业前夕才相识、并在创业后不久便陷入意见分歧的合伙人之间的差异，并为这些企业的存续寻找合适的解决方案。
利用最初提供的15,700上海银元资本，以及随后感谢维克多·沙逊爵士（Sir Victor Sassoon）慷慨捐赠而设立的康复基金（150,000美元），迄今为止，已有218名贷款申请人（连同家属约420人）获得了总额约95,000上海银元的创业贷款，并实现了自立。这些申请人部分在“国际委员会”登记，部分在马克思委员会（Committee Marx）登记。附录中附有一份按行业分类的名单。
此外，157人（连同家属共206人）找到了职位，从而不再需要福利救济。但这些数字仅涉及在“国际委员会”登记的人员。
福利救济本身包括发放住房和食品补贴，自从建立各个施食处以来发放餐券，指派医生和药物，安置

page_data.en:
-3-

Unterbringung von Kindern in Schulen, soweit sie nicht die
Jewish School besuchen konnten, Unterbringung von Kindern in
hier ansaessigen Familien, welche teilweise im Inseratenwege
ausfindig gemacht wurden, und die Bearbeitung von besonderen
Faellen, welche oft Tage in Anspruch nahmen.
Zum Beispiel erschien beim "I.C." eine Frau, deren drei Monate
alter Saeugling waehrend der Ueberfahrt nach Shanghai auf
Cow & Gate-Milk eingestellt worden war; laut zwei aerztlichen
Attesten waere das Leben des Kindes gefaehrdet, wenn ihm nicht
die gewohnte Spezialmilch weiter geboten werden kann. Da diese
jedoch sehr teuer ist (eine Buechse kostet Sh.$9.-- ) musste mit
Muehe bei einer hiesigen Firma die Lieferung von 10 Dosen zu ei-
nem bedeutend ermaessigten Preis erwirkt werden.
Ein weiterer Fall: 17 Emigranten wurde beim Lloyd Triestino das
Gepaeck nicht ausgefolgt, weil sie an Bord zwangsweise geimpft
worden waren und kein Bordgeld hatten, um die Kosten zu bezahlen.
Nach langwierigen Verhandlungen konnte das "I.C." das Gepaeck
dieser Emigranten, welches mit ca Sh.$1,000.-- belastet war, um
Sh.$400.-- ausloesen und den Emigranten zur Verfuegung stellen.
Das "I.C." war in der Lage, dem Heim in der Washing-Road, und
spaeterhin dem neu gegruendeten Heim in der Ward-Road Kohlen zu
einem bedeutend ermaessigten Preis zu verschaffen.
Am 15. Februar wurde die formelle Fuersorgearbeit, also die Auszah-
lung von Zuschuessen und die Ausgabe von tickets dem Committee
Dr. Marx ueberwiesen; beim "I.C." verblieben nurmehr die Behand-
lung der Pass-, Legitimations- und Behoerden-Angelegenheiten, die
Stellenvermittlung, ferner die administrative Behandlung der Dar-
lehnsgesuche und der damit verbundenen Auszahlungen sowie Kontrol-
len. Nichtsdestoweniger verringerte sich der Parteienverkehr kei-
neswegs, weil zahllose Ratsuchende (insbesondere beim Committee
Marx registrierte Personen) erschienen, denen auch weiterhin so
weit als moeglich geholfen wurde.
Durch persoenlichen Aufruf des Herrn Komor konnte am 20. Februar
ein "Milk-Fund" ins Leben gerufen werden, aus welchem an Klein-
kinder
page_data.zh:
-3-

儿童入学（只要他们无法进入犹太学校），将儿童安置在上海当地家庭中（部分是通过刊登广告找到的），以及处理往往需要数天时间的特殊案例。
例如，有一位妇女来到“国际委员会”，她三个月大的婴儿在前往上海的途中改喝“Cow & Gate”牌牛奶；根据两份医疗证明，如果不能继续提供惯用的特种牛奶，孩子的生命将受到威胁。由于这种牛奶非常昂贵（每罐售价9上海银元），经过努力，终于从本地一家公司以大幅降低的价格争取到了10罐的供应。
另一个案例：17名移民在劳埃德·特里斯蒂诺轮船公司（Lloyd Triestino）未能提取行李，因为他们在船上被强制接种疫苗，且没有船费来支付相关费用。经过漫长的谈判，“国际委员会”以400上海银元赎回了这批价值约1,000上海银元的移民行李，并将其交给移民。
“国际委员会”能够以大幅降低的价格为华山路（Washing-Road）的收容所，以及后来在华德路（Ward-Road）新成立的收容所提供煤炭。
2月15日，正式的福利救济工作，即发放补贴和分发餐券，移交给马克思博士委员会（Committee Dr. Marx）；“国际委员会”仅保留处理护照、身份证明和当局事务，职业介绍，以及贷款申请的行政处理、相关款项的发放和监控。尽管如此，来访人数并未减少，因为无数寻求建议者（特别是在马克思委员会登记的人员）前来求助，我们也继续尽可能地提供帮助。
通过科莫尔先生的个人呼吁，2月20日成立了一个“牛奶基金”，用于向幼儿

REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / S... REGISTRY / No. S. H. Dion. 5422(C) / 14 2 39）
Date February 14 1939.

Subject (in full) China Press dated February 11, 1939 published report regarding
the arrival in Shanghai of 85 German Jews.

Made by D.S. Lockwood. Forwarded by Inspector. E. Park

With reference to the attached cutting from the 'China
Press' dated February 11, 1939, regarding the arrival of 85
German Jews in Shanghai on February 10, 1939 on board the s.s.
'ATHOS II,' I have to report that Monsieur J. Merlant of the
Passenger Department, Messageries Maritimes, was interviewed
regarding the truth of the report. He stated that there is no
foundation in the announcement, and expressed astonishment
that the information was published without verification from
the Company's offices.

A scrutiny of the passenger manifest shows that only
seven German nationals arrived in Shanghai on that date.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / SPECIAL BRANCH）

日期 1939年2月14日。

制作人 D.S. Lockwood。由督察 E. Park 转呈

关于附上的1939年2月11日《字林西报》剪报，该报道称85名德国犹太人于1939年2月10日乘坐“阿托斯二世”号（s.s. 'ATHOS II'）轮船抵达上海，本人就此报告称，已就报道的真实性询问了法国邮船公司（Messageries Maritimes）客运部的 J. Merlant 先生。他表示，该公告毫无根据，并对该公司办事处未经核实便发布信息表示惊讶。

经仔细核对乘客名单显示，当日仅有七名德国国民抵达上海。

CHINA PRESS.
FEB 1 1 1939
85 German-Jews Flee
Germany, Land Here
By Athos Unexpected
More than 85 German-Jewish
emigres arrived in Shanghai
with the Messageries Mari-
times vessel Athos II yesterday
afternoon. It is reported that
these emigres did not leave Ger-
many legally, but fled across the
border into France, proceeding
to Marseilles, thence to Shang-
hai.
It was reported last night that
they are being temporarily ac-
commodated at the Embankment
Building.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》。
1939年2月11日
85名德籍犹太人逃离
德国，抵沪
乘坐“阿托斯”号意外抵达
昨日下午，逾85名德籍犹太移民乘坐法国邮船公司（Messageries Maritimes）的“阿托斯二世”号（Athos II）轮抵达上海。据悉，这些移民并非合法离开德国，而是越境逃往法国，随后前往马赛，再从那里来到上海。
昨晚有消息称，他们被暂时安置在外滩大厦（Embankment Building）。

S.1, Special Branch, Journal - 39
REPORT
Date February 3, 1939

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. REGISTRY
No. B. D. 5422 (C)

Subject Jewish refugees from Central Europe in Shanghai

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Crawford D.S.

It is learned that some twenty to thirty Jewish
refugees who have recently arrived in this city from
Central Europe, have applied to the Mexican Legation for
facilities to enter Mexico, since they can see no prospect
of securing employment in Shanghai.

Their applications are being considered but it is
of significance that should they be granted permission to
enter the country, they will, in the first place, be only
granted a visa allowing them to remain for one year, and
in the second, will not be permitted to work in professional
capacities (dentists, doctors, surgeons, etc.), as labourers
of any description or to employ labour.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 4 FEB. 1939）

报告
日期：1939年2月3日

上海公共租界工部局警务处
档案编号 REGISTRY
编号 B. D. 5422 (C)

主题：在上海的中欧犹太难民

撰写人：D.S. Pitts 转呈人：C. Crawford D.S.

获悉，近期从中欧抵达本市的约二三十名犹太难民已向墨西哥公使馆申请入境墨西哥的便利条件，因为他们在上海看不到获得就业的希望。

他们的申请正在审议中，但值得注意的是，即使获准入境，首先，他们仅能获得允许停留一年的签证；其次，不允许他们从事专业工作（牙医、医生、外科医生等）、任何形式的体力劳动或雇佣劳工。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处处长办公室 1939年2月4日）

Section 1, Special Branch,
January 31, 1939.

Arrival in Shanghai of Jewish Refugees from Central Europe.
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

Since last August when the general exodus from
Germany and Austria commenced, approximately 2,200 Jewish
refugees have arrived in Shanghai from those countries.
Of this number 2,040 have registered with the various
local relief committees catering for their needs and this
figure is made up of :-
1,234 men
572 women
234 children

The greater part of these refugees made the journey
to the Far East via Suez in steamers belonging to the larger
shipping companies, with German and Italian liners carrying
more than 50% of the travellers. The emigrants travelled 1st,
2nd, and 3rd Class in these ships according to the means they
possessed in Germany and Austria. Many of these emigrants
were quite wealthy before their departure, but being unable
to take anything of value with them on their journeys, paid
their fares in German Reichsmarks, a procedure which does
not constitute a breach of the prevailing currency laws.
Thus, those who were well off financially, travelled first
class; others, not quite so affluent, made the trip under
less luxurious conditions, while those who had practically
nothing came by the cheapest possible class.

A few scores of refugees travelled to Shanghai via
Siberia but the exact number cannot be determined.

98% of these unfortunates are in possession of German,
Austrian and Polish passports, the first mentioned two being
greatly in excess of the latter. The remaining 2% are

中欧犹太难民抵沪。
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

自去年8月德国和奥地利的大规模外逃开始以来，约有2,200名犹太难民从这些国家抵达上海。其中2,040人已在各类满足其需求的当地救济委员会登记，该数字构成如下：
1,234名男性
572名女性
234名儿童

这些难民中的大多数人经由苏伊士运河，乘坐大型航运公司的轮船前往远东，其中德国和意大利的班轮承运了超过50%的旅客。这些移民根据其在德国和奥地利拥有的财力，分别乘坐头等、二等和三等舱。许多移民在出发前相当富有，但由于无法在旅途中携带任何贵重物品，他们用德国马克支付船费，这一程序并不违反现行的货币法规。因此，那些经济宽裕的人乘坐头等舱；其他人虽不那么富裕，也在较为简朴的条件下旅行；而那些几乎一无所有的人则乘坐最便宜的舱位。

有几十名难民经西伯利亚前往上海，但确切人数无法确定。

这些不幸者中98%持有德国、奥地利和波兰护照，前两者的数量远多于后者。其余2%为

page_data.en:
- 2 -

classed as persons of no nationality and are mostly White
Russians who have been domiciled in Germany and Austria since
the Russian Revolution. Some of this number are in possession
of Nansen "passports" while a few have no travel papers at all.
Quite 85% of those who have arrived are without means
of their own and rely entirely on financial assistance from
relief societies to lead a hand to mouth existence. A few
refugees - not more than 25 - are well-to-do, having
transferred all their holdings and money to foreign
countries, prior to the advent of the strict currency
regulations in the Reich. These persons are not likely to
cause any trouble in Shanghai and unless they are afforded
opportunities of entering into business, are unlikely to
remain here, having sufficient funds at their disposal to
start life elsewhere.
The remainder are in possession of meagre amounts of
money. They comprise Jews of German nationality only, who
have seen the insides of concentration camps. They and
their families were granted sums ranging from U.S. $50 to
U.S. $175 according to the length of time incarcerated and
according to the number in each family. The money was
handed them by an American Jewish Relief Society with
headquarters in Paris, immediately prior to their departure
for the East.
Naturally enough under these circumstances, this
large number of refugees is finding conditions in Shanghai
far from pleasant. Few of them know any English and though
many are fully qualified in various trades and professions,
they are greatly and immediately handicapped by their lack of
knowledge of Shanghai's lingua franca. Further, positions
are difficult to secure, even supposing that every needed
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

被归类为无国籍人士，主要是自俄国革命以来一直居住在德国和奥地利的白俄人。其中一些人持有南森（Nansen）“护照”，而少数人则没有任何旅行证件。
抵达者中足足有85%没有自有资产，完全依靠救济社团的经济援助维持勉强糊口的生活。少数难民——不超过25人——生活富裕，他们在帝国实施严格的货币管制之前，已将所有财产和资金转移至国外。这些人不太可能在上海制造麻烦，除非有机会经商，否则他们也不太可能留在这里，因为他们有足够的资金在其他地方开始新生活。
其余人仅有微薄的资金。他们仅包括具有德国国籍的犹太人，这些人曾身陷集中营。他们及其家人根据被监禁的时间长短以及每个家庭的人数，获得了从50美元到175美元不等的金额。这笔钱由总部设在巴黎的美国犹太救济社在他们启程前往东方之前立即发放给他们。
在这种情况下，如此大量的难民发现上海的处境远非令人愉快，这也是自然而然的。他们中很少有人懂英语，尽管许多人在各种行业和专业方面具备充分资格，但由于缺乏对上海通用语言的了解，他们立即受到了极大的阻碍。此外，即使假设每位移民都具备所需的所有

page_data.en:
- 3 -
qualification was possessed by each and every emigrant, since
employment for foreigners is now scarcer than ever before and
competition for each vacant post from non-Jewish foreigners
is always on the increase.
The committees in charge of the refugee problem,
headed by Mr. M. SPEELMAN, are doing their very utmost to
find a satisfactory solution to a task that is growing more
difficult and more complex with the arrival of each steamer
from Europe bringing further batches of Jews. All refugees
are registered with one of the three Committees and all
particulars relating to their capabilities are recorded for
purposes of future reference.
Upon arrival in Shanghai, the new arrivals are met by
representatives of the Aid Committees, who make arrangements
for their temporary accommodation in premises located on the
1st floor of the Embankment Building, North Soochow Road, and
at 708 Whashing Road. Then, within a day or so, their
particulars are recorded, and financial assistance is given
the most deserving cases. In December, mainly through the
kindness of long established members of the local Jewish
community, these refugees were provided with the frugal needs
of existence at a rate of $60 per single person and a
proportionately less amount for married couples.
In January the figure was reduced to $55 and recipients
had to secure lodgings where they could and pay for all their
food. In other words the above mentioned sum constituted
their sole income.
Now, however, with their ever diminishing financial
resources being strained to breaking point by the needs of
the never ending stream of new-comers, the committees have
decided to cease paying a monthly dole and arrangements have
already been made to take over the former Customs training
page_data.zh:
- 3 -
资格，职位也难以获得，因为目前外国人的就业机会比以往任何时候都更加稀缺，而非犹太外国人对于每个空缺职位的竞争总是在增加。
负责处理难民问题的各委员会由M. SPEELMAN先生领导，正竭尽全力为一项随着每艘从欧洲带来新一批犹太人的轮船抵达而变得日益困难和复杂的任务寻找令人满意的解决方案。所有难民均在三个委员会之一登记，所有与其能力相关的详细信息均被记录在案，以备将来参考。
新抵达者到达上海后，由援助委员会的代表接待，并安排他们在北苏州路外滩大厦一楼和华山路708号的场所临时住宿。然后，在一两天内，记录他们的详细信息，并向最值得帮助的案例提供经济援助。去年12月，主要得益于当地犹太社区长期成员的善意，这些难民以每人60元的标准获得了维持生存所需的微薄物资，已婚夫妇的金额相应较少。
今年1月，该金额降至55元，受助者必须自行寻找住处并支付所有食物费用。换句话说，上述金额构成了他们的唯一收入。
然而现在，由于源源不断的新来者的需求使日益减少的资金资源紧张到了崩溃的边缘，各委员会已决定停止发放月度救济金，并已做出安排接管前海关培训中心，

page_data.en:
- 4 -
centre, opposite Ward Road Gaol, where between 1,200 and
1,600 refugees can be accommodated and fed. This building
is scheduled to be ready for occupation in the first few
days of February, while the centres at Embankment Building
and 708 Whashing Road will also, at a pinch, house another
450 persons. From these figures it will be observed that the
total number of immigrants is till in excess of those
that can be cared for in homes of the communal type.
In this connection it is not out of place to mention
that the Committees, by joint action, hope eventually to
confine, from the point of view of residence, all refugees
to districts North of the Soochow Creek. Whether or no this
move will be successful remains to be seen, as it is known
that little money is entering the Committees' coffers while,
when the total number of refugees only amounted to 1,600,
daily expenditure exceeded $3,000, a figure which is far from
excessive when it is considered that schooling, hospitalization,
food, lodgings, etc. etc. are included therein.
The Committees are fully aware of their difficulties
and, moreover, fully expect by the end of May - unless
measures are taken to prevent a further influx - that the
number of refugees in Shanghai will be in the region of 4,000.
These Committees are dependent upon voluntary subscriptions
and while it is true that numerous public-spirited citizens have
afforded splendid assistance in recent weeks, it is felt that
before long the problem as a whole may be far too big to be success-
fully handled by a band of voluntary workers as is the case at
present.
Looking at the less gloomy side of the picture, it is
learned that up to Friday, January 27, 1939, 246 refugees had
found employment in various concerns in Shanghai. This number
page_data.zh:
- 4 -
该中心位于华德路监狱对面，可容纳并供养1,200至1,600名难民。该建筑计划于2月初的头几天准备好供入住，而外滩大厦和华山路708号的中心在紧急情况下也可再容纳450人。从这些数字可以看出，移民总数仍然超过集体型住所能够照顾的人数。
在此方面，值得一提的是，各委员会通过联合行动，希望最终从居住角度将所有难民限制在苏州河以北的地区。这一举措是否会成功尚待观察，因为众所周知，进入委员会金库的资金很少，而当难民总数仅为1,600人时，每日支出已超过3,000元，考虑到其中包括 schooling（教育）、住院、食物、住宿等费用，这一数字绝非过高。
各委员会充分意识到他们的困难，并且，除非采取措施防止进一步涌入，否则他们完全预计到5月底，上海的难民数量将达到4,000人左右。
这些委员会依赖自愿捐款，虽然确实有许多热心公民在最近几周提供了极好的帮助，但人们认为，不久之后，整个问题可能太大，无法像目前这样由一群志愿工作人员成功处理。
从较不悲观的一面来看，据悉，截至1939年1月27日星期五，已有246名难民在上海的各类企业中找到了工作。这一数字

page_data.en:
- 5 -
includes those who have been established in different types of
business with money loaned by the Relief Committees, while those
who have secured posts have filled vacancies and have not displaced
other employees.

It is still too early to judge whether the fact of
these refugees securing employment in Shanghai is likely
to affect the positions of other local foreigners in
employment. As far as can be ascertained at present, there
has been no effect at all but, it is quite likely in the
future, that many of the immigrants who are tradesmen, will, for
the sake of a crust of bread, commence undertaking tasks at
wages that may be far below those received by foreigners
now doing such work. Attached hereto are rough copies
of lists secured from the Relief Committees of names,
addresses and professions of a few of the newly arrived
refugees. From these it will be seen that there are printer,
bookbinders, window dressers, engineers, architects,
electricians, welders, plumbers, mechanics, technical experts,
road constructors, cable layers, builders, joiners, fitters,
surveyors, chemists, experts in wood, gas, metal and diesel
motors, lock-smiths, chauffeurs, upholsterers, etc., etc.
It is also known that others - not listed - are grocers,
sausage manufacturers, bank clerks, shipping clerks, interpreters,
etc., etc.

Most of the trades followed by the above individuals
are those performed by Chinese in Shanghai and it is most
difficult to imagine, for instance, a foreign lock-smith
upsetting the labour market from a foreign angle as things
exist at present. On the other hand such men as surveyors,
experts in road laying, etc., etc., provided they have the
necessary language qualifications, could and might well be
page_data.zh:
- 5 -
包括那些利用救济委员会贷款在不同类型企业中立足的人，而那些获得职位的人填补了空缺，并未取代其他雇员。

现在判断这些难民在上海获得就业是否会影响其他在当地就业的外国人的地位还为时过早。就目前所能查明的情况而言，没有任何影响，但在未来，许多身为技工的移民很可能为了糊口，开始以远低于目前从事此类工作的外国人所获得的工资承担任务。随函附上从救济委员会获取的几名新抵达难民的姓名、地址和职业清单的粗略副本。从中可以看出，其中有印刷工、装订工、橱窗布置师、工程师、建筑师、电工、焊工、水管工、机械师、技术专家、道路建设工、电缆铺设工、建筑工、木工、装配工、测量员、化学家、木材、煤气、金属和柴油发动机专家、锁匠、司机、室内装饰师等。
还已知其他人——未列在名单上——是杂货商、香肠制造商、银行职员、航运职员、翻译等。

上述个人从事的大多数行业都是上海由中国人从事的行业，很难想象，例如，一名外国锁匠会在目前的情况下从外国人的角度扰乱劳动力市场。另一方面，像测量员、铺路专家等人，只要他们具备必要的语言能力，完全有可能被

page_data.en:
- 6 -
engaged by reputable local firms at far lower salaries to
the exclusion of the present employees.
As mentioned higher, it is perhaps a little too
premature to make a survey of the manner in which the
foreign labour market is likely to be affected, but
arrangements will be made to keep in continual touch with
the responsible officers of the Relief Committees in order
that all new aspects and phases of the refugee question may
be brought to your notice.

Certified true copy
H. C. Randley
THJ/●
page_data.zh:
- 6 -
信誉良好的本地公司以远低于现有雇员的薪水聘用，从而排挤现有雇员。
如上所述，对外国劳动力市场可能受到影响的方式进行调查或许为时过早，但将做出安排，与救济委员会的负责官员保持持续联系，以便将难民问题的所有新方面和新阶段提请注意。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE REGISTRY
File No.
No. S. B. D. 5422(c)
Date 1/31/39
Date January 31, 1939.

Subject Arrival in Shanghai of Jewish Refugees from Central Europe.

Made by D. S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Crawford. S. I.

Since last August when the general exodus from
Germany and Austria commenced, approximately 2,200 Jewish
refugees have arrived in Shanghai from those countries.
Of this number 2,040 have registered with the various
local relief committees catering for their needs and this
figure is made up of :-
1,234 men
572 women
234 children

The greater part of these refugees made the journey
to the Far East via Suez in steamers belonging to the larger
shipping companies, with German and Italian liners carrying
more than 50% of the travellers. The emigrants travelled 1st,
2nd and 3rd Class in these ships according to the means they
possessed in Germany and Austria. Many of these emigrants
were quite wealthy before their departure, but being unable
to take anything of value with them on their journeys, paid
their fares in German Reichsmarks, a procedure which does
not constitute a breach of the prevailing currency laws.
Thus, those who were well off financially, travelled first
class; others, not quite so affluent, made the trip under
less luxurious conditions, while those who had practically
nothing came by the cheapest possible class.

A few scores of refugees travelled to Shanghai via
Siberia but the exact number cannot be determined.

98% of these unfortunates are in possession of German,
Austrian and Polish passports, the first mentioned two being
greatly in excess of the latter. The remaining 2% are

日期 1939年1月31日。

事由 中欧犹太难民抵达上海。

撰写人 D. S. 皮茨 (Pitts) 呈报人 C. 克劳福德 (Crawford). S. I.

自去年八月德国和奥地利的大规模外逃开始以来，约有2,200名犹太难民从这些国家抵达上海。其中2,040人已向当地各救济委员会登记以寻求援助，该数字构成如下：
1,234名男性
572名女性
234名儿童

这些难民中大部分经由苏伊士运河乘坐大型航运公司的轮船前往远东，其中德国和意大利的班轮承运了超过50%的旅客。这些移民根据其在德国和奥地利拥有的财力，分别乘坐头等、二等和三等舱。许多移民在出发前相当富有，但由于无法在旅途中携带任何贵重物品，他们使用德国 Reichsmarks（帝国马克）支付船费，这一程序并不违反现行的货币法规。因此，那些经济宽裕的人乘坐头等舱；其他人虽不那么富裕，也在较为简朴的条件下旅行；而那些几乎一无所有的人则乘坐最便宜的舱位。

有几十名难民经西伯利亚前往上海，但确切人数无法确定。

这些不幸者中98%持有德国、奥地利和波兰护照，前两者的数量远远超过后者。其余2%为

classed as persons of no nationality and are mostly White
Russians who have been domiciled in Germany and Austria since
the Russian Revolution. Some of this number are in possession
of Nansen "passports" while a few have no travel papers at all.
    Quite 85% of those who have arrived are without means
of their own and rely entirely on financial assistance from
relief societies to lead a hand to mouth existence. A few
refugees - not more than 25 - are well-to-do, having
transferred all their holdings and money to foreign
countries, prior to the advent of the strict currency
regulations in the Reich. These persons are not likely to
cause any trouble in Shanghai and unless they are afforded
opportunities of entering into business, are unlikely to
remain here, having sufficient funds at their disposal to
start life elsewhere.
    The remainder are in possession of meagre amounts of
money. They comprise Jews of German nationality only, who
have seen the insides of concentration camps. They and
their families were granted sums ranging from U.S. $50 to
U.S. $175 according to the length of time incarcerated and
according to the number in each family. The money was
handed them by an American Jewish Relief Society with
headquarters in Paris, immediately prior to their departure
for the East.
    Naturally enough under these circumstances, this
large number of refugees is finding conditions in Shanghai
far from pleasant. Few of them know any English and though
many are fully qualified in various trades and professions,

被归类为无国籍人士，主要是自俄国革命以来定居在德国和奥地利的白俄罗斯人。其中一些人持有南森 (Nansen) “护照”，而少数人则没有任何旅行证件。
    抵达者中整整85%身无分文，完全依靠救济团体的财政援助维持勉强糊口的生活。少数难民——不超过25人——生活富裕，他们在帝国实施严格的货币管制之前，已将所有资产和资金转移到国外。这些人不太可能在上海制造麻烦，除非获得经商机会，否则他们不太可能留在这里，因为他们拥有足够的资金在其他地方开始新生活。
    其余人手中仅有微薄的资金。他们仅由具有德国国籍的犹太人组成，这些人曾身陷集中营。他们及其家人根据被囚禁时间的长短以及每个家庭的人数，获得了从50美元到175美元不等的金额。这笔钱由总部设在巴黎的美国犹太救济协会在他们启程前往东方之前立即交给他们。
    在这种情况下，如此大量的难民发现上海的条件远非令人愉快，这是很自然的。他们中很少有人懂英语，尽管许多人在各种行业和专业方面具备完全的资格，

they are greatly and immediately handicapped by their lack of
knowledge of Shanghai's lingua franca. Further, positions
are difficult to secure, even supposing that every needed
qualification was possessed by each and every emigrant, since
employment for foreigners is now scarcer than ever before
and competition for each vacant post from non-Jewish
foreigners is always on the increase.

The committees in charge of the refugee problem,
headed by Mr. M. SPEELMAN, are doing their very utmost to
find a satisfactory solution to a task that is growing more
difficult and more complex with the arrival of each steamer
from Europe bringing further batches of Jews. All refugees
are registered with one of the three Committees and all
particulars relating to their capabilities are recorded for
purposes of future reference.

Upon arrival in Shanghai, the new arrivals are met by
representatives of the Aid Committees, who make arrangements
for their temporary accomodation in premises located on the
1st floor of the Embankment Building, North Soochow Road, and
at 708 Whashing Road. Then, within a day or so, their
particulars are recorded, and financial assistance is given
the most deserving cases. In December, mainly through the
kindness of long established members of the local Jewish
community, these refugees were provided with the frugal needs
of existence at a ratio of $60 per single person and a
proportionately less amount for married couples.

In January the figure was reduced to $55 and recipients
had to secure lodgings where they could and pay for all their
food. In other words the above mentioned sum constituted

负责难民问题的各委员会由 M. SPEELMAN 先生领导，正竭尽全力为一项随着每一艘从欧洲驶来、载着新一批犹太难民的轮船抵达而变得愈发困难和复杂的任务寻找令人满意的解决方案。所有难民均在三个委员会之一登记，其能力相关的所有详细信息均被记录在案，以备将来参考。

新抵达者到达上海后，由援助委员会的代表接待，并安排他们在北苏州路堤岸大厦（Embankment Building）一楼和华盛路 708 号的场所临时住宿。随后，在一两天内，他们的详细信息被记录在案，并向最值得帮助的情况提供经济援助。十二月，主要得益于当地犹太社区长期成员的好意，这些难民获得了维持生存所需的微薄物资，标准为单身每人 60 美元，已婚夫妇则按比例减少。

一月，该金额减至 55 美元，受助者需自行设法解决住宿并支付所有食物费用。换言之，上述金额构成了

their sole income.
Now, however, with their ever diminishing financial
resources being strained to breaking point by the needs of
the never ending stream of new-comers, the committees have
decided to cease paying a monthly dole and arrangements have
already been made to take over the former Customs training
centre, opposite Ward Road Gaol, where between 1,200 and
1,500 refugees can be accomodated and fed. This building
is scheduled to be ready for occupation in the first few
days of February, while the centres at Embankment Building
and 703 Whashing Road will also, at a pinch, house another
450 persons. From these figures it will be observed that
the total number of immigrants is still in excess of those
that can be cared for in homes of the communal type.
In this connection it is not out of place to mention
that the Committees, by joint action, hope eventually to
confine, from the point of view of residence, all refugees
to districts North of the Soochow Creek. Whether or no this
move will be successful remains to be seen, as it is known
that little money is entering the Committees' coffers while,
when the total number of refugees only amounted to 1,600,
daily expenditure exceeded $3,000, a figure which is far from
excessive when it is considered that schooling, hospitalization,
food, lodgings, etc. etc. are included therein.
The Committees are fully aware of their difficulties
and, moreover, fully expect by the end of May - unless
measures are taken to prevent a further influx - that the
number of refugees in Shanghai will be in the region of 4,000.

然而，现在由于源源不断的新来者的需求使本就日益减少的资金资源紧张到了崩溃的边缘，各委员会已决定停止发放月度救济金，并已做出安排接管位于华德路监狱对面的前海关培训中心，该处可容纳并供养 1,200 至 1,500 名难民。该建筑计划于二月初的头几天准备就绪以供入住，而堤岸大厦和华盛路 703 号的中心在紧急情况下也可再容纳 450 人。从这些数字可以看出，移民总数仍然超过集体型住所能够照顾的人数。
在此方面，值得一提的是，各委员会通过联合行动，希望最终从居住角度将所有难民限制在苏州河以北的地区。这一举措是否成功尚待观察，因为众所周知，进入委员会金库的资金寥寥无几，而当难民总数仅为 1,600 人时，每日支出已超过 3,000 美元，考虑到其中包含 schooling（教育）、hospitalization（住院医疗）、食物、住宿等费用，这一数字绝非过高。
各委员会充分意识到其困难，并且完全预计，除非采取措施防止进一步涌入，否则到五月底，上海的难民人数将达到 4,000 人左右。

These Committees are dependent upon voluntary subscriptions
and while it is true that numerous public-spirited
citizens have afforded splendid assistance in recent weeks,
it is felt that before long the problem as a whole may be
far too big to be successfully handled by a band of
voluntary workers as is the case at present.

    Looking at the less gloomy side of the picture, it
is learned that up to Friday, January 27, 1939, 246
refugees had found employment in various concerns in
Shanghai. This number includes those who have been
established in different types of businesses with money
loaned by the Relief Committees, while those who have
secured posts have filled vacancies and have not displaced
other employees.

    It is still too early to judge whether the fact of
these refugees securing employment in Shanghai is likely
to affect the positions of other local foreigners in
employment. As far as can be ascertained at present,
there has been no effect at all but, it is quite likely in
the future, that many of the immigrants who are tradesmen,
will, for the sake of a crust of bread, commence undertaking
tasks at wages that may be far below those received by
foreigners now doing such work. Attached hereto are rough
copies of lists secured from the Relief Committees of names,
addresses and professions of a few of the newly arrived
refugees. From these it will be seen that there are printers,
bookbinders, window dressers, engineers, architects,
electricians, welders, plumbers, mechanics, technical experts,

从较为乐观的一面来看，据悉截至 1939 年 1 月 27 日星期五，已有 246 名难民在上海各类企业中找到了工作。这一数字包括那些利用救济委员会贷款在不同类型企业中立足的人，而那些获得职位的人填补了空缺，并未排挤其他雇员。

现在判断这些难民在上海就业是否会影响其他在当地就业的外国人的地位还为时过早。就目前所能查明的情况而言，没有任何影响，但在未来，许多身为技工的移民很可能为了糊口，开始以远低于目前从事此类工作的外国人所获工资的水平承接任务。随函附上从救济委员会获取的部分新到难民的姓名、地址和职业名单的粗略副本。从中可以看出，其中有印刷工、装订工、橱窗陈列师、工程师、建筑师、电工、焊工、水管工、机械师、技术专家、

It is also known that others - not listed - are grocers,
sausage manufacturers, bank clerks, shipping clerks,
interpreters, etc., etc.
    Most of the trades followed by the above individuals
are those performed by Chinese in Shanghai and it is most
difficult to imagine, for instance, a foreign lock-smith
upsetting the labour market from a foreign angle as things
exist at present. On the other hand such men as surveyors,
experts in road laying, etc., etc., provided they have the
necessary language qualifications, could and might well be
engaged by reputable local firms at far lower salaries to
the exclusion of the present employees.
    As mentioned higher, it is perhaps a little too
premature to make a survey of the manner in which the
foreign labour market is likely to be affected, but
arrangements will be made to keep in continual touch with
the responsible officers of the Relief Committees in order
that all new aspects and phases of the refugee question may
be brought to your notice.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No............
S.I, Special Branch, xxxxx
REPORT
Date January 11, 1939.
Subject Arrival of Jewish refugees from Germany and Austria
Made by/ and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

Further to Special Branch report dated December 8,
1938 when it was stated that 500 Jewish refugees had
arrived in Shanghai 900 have arrived in the interim, and
the total number at present in Shanghai is 1,400. Of the
new arrivals 300 to 400 are accommodated in the Embankment
Building. The exact number cannot be ascertained as the
refugees are constantly changing from the building to
addresses in the Eastern district. The remainder are
accommodated in foreign style houses on Wayside Road,
Baikal Road and vicinity. The relief committee is at
present in desperate straits, as most of the money received
has been exhausted and further subscriptions cannot be
relied upon. With the arrival of further batches, expected
daily, the situation will become much more serious. At
present, premises located at 81 Wayside Road are being
extensively altered, and it is expected that 1,500 refugees
may be accommodated here. Of the refugee children, 60 are
being taught at the Shanghai Jewish School, Seymour Road
which at present is overcrowded. The adults are attending
classes in English supervised by voluntary teachers at the
Museum Road synagogue. The economic problem involved is
difficult. The average White Russian is content with a
sum sufficient to meet the bare necessities of life, but
the average Jewish refugee is receiving good food and
comparative comfort free of charge, so that to persuade
them to accept employment which will not guarantee them
more than their present material comforts will be a
difficult task, but several have been placed in employment.

日期 1939年1月11日。
主题 来自德国和奥地利的犹太难民的抵达
撰写人/转发人 督察克劳福德 (D.I. Crawford)

继1938年12月8日的特别科报告之后，
当时指出已有500名犹太难民
抵达上海，在此期间又有900人抵达，
目前在上海的总数为1,400人。在新抵达者中，
有300至400人被安置在堤岸大厦
（Embankment Building）。确切数字无法确定，因为
难民不断从该大厦搬往东区各地址。其余人员
被安置在韦思德路（Wayside Road）、
贝加尔路（Baikal Road）及附近的外国式住宅中。救济委员会目前
处境极为艰难，因为收到的大部分资金
已耗尽，且无法指望进一步的捐款。随着预计
每日都会抵达的更多批次难民，局势将变得
更加严峻。目前，位于韦思德路81号的场所
正在进行大规模改建，预计可在此安置
1,500名难民。在难民儿童中，有60名正在
西摩路的上海犹太学校就读，该校目前
已人满为患。成年人则在博物馆路犹太会堂
参加由志愿教师监督的英语课程。所涉及的
经济问题十分棘手。一般的白俄满足于仅够
维持基本生活需求的金额，但一般的犹太难民
却免费获得良好的食物和相对舒适的生活条件，
因此要说服他们接受一份不能保证提供比目前
物质享受更优厚待遇的工作将是一项艰巨的任务，
不过已有数人得以就业。

At present figures are not available, but will be given
when ascertained. Another disturbing feature is that
the recent arrivals are inclined to look down on the
local Jewish community, comprised for the most part of
Russian Jews, to whom they consider themselves superior.
To add to an already complicated problem, a percentage
of the new arrivals have contrived to bring their
valuables (mostly jewels) to Shanghai, but as they are
naturally reticent concerning their possessions the
percentage is not known. Enquiries are proceeding
and a further report will be forwarded when information
is available.

C. S. 6, Special Branch
REPORT
Date...January 9, 1939.

Subject......Jewish Refugees - Arrival in Shanghai.

Made by D. S. Hocking        Forwarded by      Inspector E. Paff

On 31-12-38, 338 German, Roumanian, Hungarian and
Czecho-Slovakian Jews landed in Shanghai from Europe, 259
travelling by the s.s. "Conte Rosso" and 79 by the s.s. "Potsdam."
Other than the full names, no details are available concerning
these arrivals, in most cases the Shanghai address is given
C/o The Committee of Welfare of German Jews. Jewish refugees
are also arriving in Shanghai from Dairen by the Dairen Kisen
Kaisha vessels but no accurate check can be made of their
numbers owing to the fact that they are not stated on passenger
lists to be Jews, and it can only be assumed that many passengers
of European nationality reach Dairen via Siberia.

D. S. Hocking
D. S.

D.C. (Special Branch).
P. A. to D. C. (Sp. Br.)

1938年12月31日，338名德国、罗马尼亚、匈牙利和
捷克斯洛伐克犹太人在上海从欧洲登陆，其中259人
乘坐“罗索伯爵”号轮船（s.s. "Conte Rosso"），79人乘坐“波茨坦”号轮船（s.s. "Potsdam"）。
除全名外，关于这些抵达者的详细信息一无所知，在大多数情况下，上海的地址列为
转交德国犹太人福利委员会。犹太难民也通过大连汽船株式会社
（Dairen Kisen Kaisha）的船只从大连抵达上海，但由于乘客名单上
并未注明其为犹太人，因此无法对其人数进行准确核查，只能推测许多
欧洲国籍的乘客经西伯利亚抵达大连。

D. S. Hocking

Date December 13, 1938.
Subject Alleged attitude of the Japanese Authorities towards Jewish refugees.

Made by.................................... Forwarded by....................................

It would appear from information received from
Mr. A. Pourin during the course of a casual telephone conver-
sation to-day that the Japanese Authorities express deep con-
cern regarding the continued influx in Shanghai of Jewish
refugees from Europe, among whom they suspect the presence of
communistic and pro-communistic elements. According to Pourin,
North China and Japan have been closed to these refugees, and
measures are being discussed as to what could be done in Shangh-
ai in this respect. Among the measures suggested was the
establishment of a passport examination system on ships
arriving in Shanghai. It was also suggested that Jewish
refugees residing in the area North of Creek must be in
possession of certificates of "political reliability" from
the local German Consulate or other Consulates concerned.

Certified true copy.
H. C. Sandley

REPORT
Date. December. 8.. 1938.

Subject....... Arrival of Jewish refugees from Germany and Austria.

Made by....................................Forwarded by....................................

Approximately 500 Jewish refugees from Germany and
Austria have arrived in Shanghai since the beginning of August
1938. Most of the refugees comprise single people or childless
married couples, there being very few children among the
number. They are for the most part educated and cultured,
with merchants predominating and a sprinkling of lawyers,
doctors and musicians. Up to the present through the
generosity of the local Jewish community headed by Sir Elly
Kadoorie and his son Mr. Horace Kadoorie, the refugees have
been provided with the necessities of life, at a ratio of
$60 per month for a single person, and at a proportionately
less rate for a married couple.

The majority of the married people are accommodated
in the Eastern District in foreign style houses on Wayside Road,
Baikal Road and vicinity. The single men are all accommodated
in the former Foreign Women's Home on Whashing Road. Here,
they are being taught the English language under the guidance
of a refugee lawyer with an excellent knowledge of the language.
The children are receiving free tuition and meals at the
Shanghai Jewish School, Seymour Road. All arrangements and
relief work pertaining to the refugees are being carried out
by two committees, the German Committee and the Austrian
Committee. Efforts which will probably be successful are being
made to amalgamate the two committees. Apart from the above
mentioned relief work, help has been given to establish individual
refugees or couples in small business or professional ventures,
by means of loans, for instance, doctors have been given the
money necessary to purchase instruments.

事由....... 来自德国和奥地利的犹太难民抵达。

制作人....................................转呈人....................................

自1938年8月初以来，约有500名来自德国和奥地利的犹太难民抵达上海。大多数难民为单身人士或无子女的已婚夫妇，其中儿童极少。他们大多受过教育且有文化修养，以商人为主，兼有少量律师、医生和音乐家。截至目前，在由埃利·卡多里爵士 (Sir Elly Kadoorie) 及其子贺拉斯·卡多里先生 (Mr. Horace Kadoorie) 领导的本地犹太社区的慷慨资助下，难民们已获得生活必需品，标准为单身人士每月60美元，已婚夫妇则按比例减少。

大多数已婚人士被安置在东区外摆渡路 (Wayside Road)、贝加尔路 (Baikal Road) 及附近地区的外国式住宅中。所有单身男子均被安置在华盛路 (Whashing Road) 的前外籍妇女收容所。在这里，他们在一位精通英语的难民律师的指导下学习英语。儿童在西摩路 (Seymour Road) 的上海犹太学校接受免费教育和膳食。所有与难民有关的安排和救济工作均由两个委员会执行，即德国委员会和奥地利委员会。目前正努力合并这两个委员会，且很可能成功。除上述救济工作外，还通过贷款等方式帮助个别难民或夫妇开展小本生意或专业活动，例如，向医生提供购买医疗器械所需的资金。

the present type already in Shanghai, it is possible that

constitute a major problem.

aid of the Jewish communities in England and the U.S.A.

committees.

The following figures quoted are all approximate:-

1) Total number of arrivals in Shanghai - 17,000.
