page_data.en:
39

Japanese to Restrict Jewish
Immigration into Hongkew

All Refugees to Register Before August 22 ; New Arrivals
Not to Be Allowed to Live in Japanese-Occupied Areas

JEWISH refugees arriving in Shanghai after August 21, will not be permitted to live in Hongkew, according to a memorandum sent to the committee in charge of Jewish refugees here by the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters. The Japanese authorities point out that, hitherto, a humanitarian attitude has been adopted and no restrictions were placed on the settlement of Jewish refugees in Japanese-occupied territories. Attention is drawn to the fact, however, that a dearth of houses exists following the destruction caused by the 1937 hostilities and that after due consideration, the Japanese authorities had decided to curtail a further influx into the districts in question.

It is also pointed out that even the return of former Japanese residents of Shanghai is restricted, apart from the fact that the Chinese are only permitted to return in small numbers. An influx of a large number of refugees, the memorandum states, would have a direct bearing in numerous ways on the reconstruction plan of war-torn areas and the question of restricting further influx has been studied all the more so as Jewish circles here had made it clear that further immigration should be discouraged.

Taking into consideration the interests of all parties concerned, the memorandum continues, the Japanese authorities have come to the conclusion that temporarily a further Jewish influx should be stopped pending the study of the possibility of accommodating a greater number in future.

It has therefore been decided that a directory of Jewish refugees be created and that for this purpose, all Jewish refugees residing in Hongkew will fill in a questionnaire in duplicate, which is then to be forwarded to the Japanese authorities through the committee. The Japanese authorities will consider these application forms carefully and will return one of the two copies to those residents who will be permitted to remain in Hongkew whilst those who shall continue to reside there without this permit or those who will have established themselves after August 22, date on which all questionnaires must be in the hands of the Japanese authorities, may be asked to move out of the district, the memorandum adds.

The committee is requested to see to it that the filling out of these forms is carried out efficiently and speedily and to urge new arrivals not to move into Hongkew, in compliance with the Japanese decision.

Japanese Claim Right

Questioned at the press conference yesterday by what right the Japanese had adopted this policy of limiting residence in areas north of Soochow Creek, the spokesman replied that that portion of the International Settlement was controlled by the Japanese—who could legislate as they pleased—by reason of military conquest. No spokesman would admit that the Powers would admit this right, but the naval spokesman pointed out that the Japanese had notified the Consular Body of the procedure which they proposed to adopt.

In reply to a correspondent, who asked whether Britons or other nationals might be subject to a similar regulation, as a matter of precedent, the spokesman replied that regulation of the refugees was an emergency measure based on actuality, not on principle.

The spokesman adduced further that more arrivals of refugees, who intended to open businesses would threaten the livelihood of those residing in the occupied portion of the area, which included Chapei—this was the viewpoint, he added, of the Jewish committee. The committee did not want a further influx of refugees. The spokesman in continuing, said that the Jewish people living in the area, excluding those in camps, were about one tenth of the Japanese residing there and the authorities feared friction between the two communities. Restrictions existed, he added, on the number of Japanese allowed to come to Shanghai.

Memorandum Causes Stir

The memorandum was reported to have created a considerable stir in refugee committee circles in view of the fact that a new camp, capable of accommodating 2,500 persons, has just been completed. A committee meeting was held on Thursday afternoon and it was understood that further conferences with the Japanese authorities would be arranged.

The "North-China Daily News" was unable to ascertain whether the Japanese would permit the use of the new Pingliang Road camp, although it was presumed in responsible quarters that the camps situated North of the creek would not be interfered with provided that applications from residents would be forthcoming as required.
page_data.zh:
39

日本人限制犹太人
移民进入虹口

所有难民须在8月22日前登记；新抵者
不得居住于日军占领区

据日本海军陆战队司令部向负责此处犹太难民的委员会发送的一份备忘录称，8月21日之后抵达上海的犹太难民将不被允许居住在虹口。日本当局指出，迄今为止，当局一直采取人道主义态度，未对犹太难民在日军占领区的定居施加任何限制。然而，提请注意的是，由于1937年战事造成的破坏，房屋极度短缺，经慎重考虑，日本当局决定限制难民进一步涌入上述地区。

备忘录还指出，甚至前上海日本居民的返回都受到限制，更不用说中国人仅被允许少量返回。备忘录称，大量难民的涌入将在多方面直接影响战乱地区的重建计划；鉴于此处的犹太界人士已明确表示应劝阻进一步移民，因此对限制进一步涌入的问题进行了更为深入的研究。

备忘录继续称，考虑到所有相关方的利益，日本当局得出结论，在研究未来容纳更多人的可能性期间，暂时停止犹太人的进一步涌入。

因此，决定建立一份犹太难民名册，为此目的，所有居住在虹口的犹太难民需填写一式两份的调查表，然后通过委员会转交日本当局。日本当局将仔细审查这些申请表，并将其中一份副本退还给获准留在虹口的居民；而那些在没有此许可证的情况下继续居住在那里的人，或在8月22日（所有调查表必须送达日本当局的日期）之后定居的人，可能会被要求搬离该地区，备忘录补充道。

委员会被要求确保高效、迅速地完成表格填写工作，并敦促新抵达者遵照日本方面的决定，不要搬入虹口。

日方声称拥有权利

在昨天的新闻发布会上，当被问及日本依据何种权利采取这项限制苏州河以北地区居住的政策时，发言人回答说，国际租界的该部分区域因军事征服而由日本控制——日本可以随心所欲地制定法律。没有发言人会承认列强会承认这一权利，但海军发言人指出，日本已将其拟采取的程序通知了领事团。

在回答一位记者关于作为先例，英国人或其他国籍人士是否可能受到类似规定约束的提问时，发言人回答说，对难民的管制是一项基于现实情况而非原则的紧急措施。

发言人进一步提出，更多打算经商的难民抵达，将威胁到居住在该地区被占领部分（包括闸北）的人们的生计——他补充说，这是犹太委员会的观点。委员会不希望难民进一步涌入。发言人接着说，居住在该地区的犹太人（难民营中的人除外）约占当地日本人的十分之一，当局担心两个社区之间会发生摩擦。他补充说，对允许来上海的日本人的数量也有限制。

备忘录引起轰动

据报道，这份备忘录在难民委员会圈内引起了相当大的骚动，因为一个能容纳2,500人的新难民营刚刚建成。周四下午举行了一次委员会会议，据悉将安排与日本当局进行进一步会谈。

《字林西报》无法查明日本方面是否允许使用新的平凉路难民营，尽管有关方面推测，只要居民按要求提出申请，位于苏州河以北的难民营就不会受到干扰。

page_data.en:
23224

Members of the refugee committee
declined to make a statement yester-
day but were confident that the
Japanese authorities, who are known
for their attitude towards the refugees
in that they consider all people equal
and sympathize with the Jewish re-
fugees, would assist as much as pos-
sible in the smooth operation of
settling Jewish emigrees who are ex-
pected to arrive in future.

Shortage of Houses

It was presumed that the memo-
randum was issued as Japanese ar-
rivals here had found it increasingly
difficult to find suitable accommoda-
tion in Hongkew as nearly all un-
damaged houses were at present being
occupied by Jewish refugees, with the
result that rents have increased con-
siderably and that accommodation has
become scarce. It was furthermore
felt that these restrictions would be
of a temporary nature and would be
lifted as soon as the reconstruction of
Hongkew and other districts north of
the creek would have got under way.
Hitherto, the Japanese authorities
have shown themselves extremely
satisfied with the settlement of Jewish
refugees in those areas as the latter
have opened business firms and shops
and have thus somewhat helped in
the return of more normal conditions.
Although no exact figures were
available, a conservative estimate
places the number of Jewish refugees
who are expected to arrive here be-
fore the end of the year at 5.000, all
of whom will have to be accom-
modated South of the creek in the
event that the restrictions are not
lifted within a month or two. Due
to the shortage of accommodation
here the committee is faced with the
almost insurmountable problem of
finding rooms and houses for about
5.000 persons.
It was not anticipated that the
Japanese authorities would request
any Jewish refugees residing in
Hongkew before August 21 to leave,
although in accordance with the word-
ing of the memorandum they reserve
the right to do so.

（批：8/9, 18）
page_data.zh:
23224

难民委员会成员昨日
拒绝发表声明，但他们
确信，以对难民态度著
称的日本当局——他们
视人人平等并同情犹太
难民——将尽可能协助
顺利安置预计未来抵达
的犹太移民。

房屋短缺

据推测，发布该备忘录
是因为抵达此地的日本人
发现越来越难以在虹口找
到合适的住所，因为几乎
所有未受损的房屋目前都
被犹太难民占用，导致租
金大幅上涨，住房变得稀
缺。此外，人们认为这些
限制将是临时性的，一旦
虹口及苏州河以北其他地
区的重建工作开始，限制
就会解除。迄今为止，日
本当局对犹太难民在这些
地区的定居表示极为满
意，因为后者开设了商行
和店铺，从而在一定程度上
帮助恢复了较为正常的状
况。虽然没有确切的数
字，但保守估计，预计在
年底前抵达此地的犹太难
民人数为5,000人，如果
限制在一两个月内不解
除，所有这些人都将被安
置在苏州河以南。由于此
处住房短缺，委员会面临
着为约5,000人寻找房间
和房屋的几乎不可克服的
难题。
预计日本当局不会要求
8月21日之前居住在虹口
的任何犹太难民离开，尽
管根据备忘录的措辞，他
们保留这样做的权利。

（批：8/9, 18）

page_data.en:
Jewish Refugees Must
Register To Reside Or
Do Business In Hongkew

All Those Not Registered By August 21 Will Not
Be Allowed To Trade Or Live In Japanese
Defence Sector; New Arrivals Barred

MEASURE TAKEN NOT TO THREATEN
LIVELIHOOD OF EARLY ARRIVALS

Taking action to curb the influx of Jewish emigrés into
areas north of the Soochow Creek, the Japanese Naval Landing
Party authorities announced yesterday that all Jewish emigrés
residing in the Japanese Defence Sector or engaged in business
there or intending to reside there or transfer their domicile to
that area must register with the Jewish Immigrants Relief
Committee by August 21.

Anyone failing to register by that date and all new arrivals
will not be permitted to reside or do business in Hongkew,
Wayside, Yangtzepoo and Chapei, the Navy spokesman announc-
ed at the Press Conference yesterday afternoon.

The registration of the emigrants
will commence to-day. All will be
required to fill in two forms,
which will be provided by the
Jewish Immigrants Relief Commit-
tee. These forms will be present-
ed through the Committee to the
office of the Japanese Resident
Naval Officer in Shanghai for au-
thorization. Identification cards
will be issued to all those
who register by August 21, and
only those in possession of the
identification cards will be allowed
to do business or reside north of
the Soochow Creek.

The Navy spokesman explained
that the reason that this action is
being taken is the fact that in the
northern and eastern districts of
the Settlement there are already
between 4,000 and 5,000 Jewish
refugees in residence and engaged
in business, apart from those in re-
fugee camps.

He contended that the Jewish
Refugee Committee had pointed
out that a further influx of Jewish
refugees into Shanghai would
threaten the livelihood of those
already here. The spokesman also
stated that the Jewish Refugee Com-
mittee had repeatedly expressed
the wish whereby a constructive
step be taken to curb the influx.

Friction Feared

Moreover, the spokesman con-
tended, the fact that the Jewish
population in the Japanese Defence
Sector was about one-tenth of the
Japanese population of Shanghai,
has led to a fear of friction be-
tween these two communities. He
added that this was a temporary
measure taken at the present time
in view of the fact that normal
conditions had not been restored to
Shanghai and due to the fact that
there is at present an acute short-
age of houses.

"At present, there is even a
restriction on the number of Japan-
ese entering Shanghai," the spokes-
man pointed out.

In reply to questions, the spokes-
man maintained that this was an
emergency measure due to present
conditions and further taken upon
the request of the Jewish Refugee
Committee for definite action to be
taken.
page_data.zh:
犹太难民必须
登记方可在虹口
居住或经商

8月21日前未登记者不得在
日本防区贸易或居住；新抵者被禁

采取措施不威胁
早抵者的生计

为遏制犹太移民涌入苏州河以北地区，日本海军陆战队当局昨日宣布，所有居住在日本防区、在该地区经商、或打算居住或将户籍迁入该地区的犹太移民，必须在8月21日前向犹太移民救济委员会登记。

海军发言人在昨日下午的新闻发布会上宣布，凡在该日期前未登记的人员及所有新抵达者，将不被允许在虹口、汇山（Wayside）、杨树浦和闸北居住或经商。

移民登记将于今日开始。所有人都
需填写两份表格，这些表格将由
犹太移民救济委员会提供。这些
表格将通过委员会提交给上海日
本驻在海军武官办公室以获得批
准。身份证将颁发给所有在8月
21日前登记的人，只有持有身份
证的人才被允许在苏州河以北经
商或居住。

海军发言人解释说，采取这一行
动的原因是，在租界的北部和东
部地区，除了难民营中的人之外，
已有4,000至5,000名犹太难民居
住并从事商业活动。

他声称，犹太难民委员会曾指
出，犹太难民进一步涌入上海将
威胁到已在此地的人们的生计。
发言人还表示，犹太难民委员会
曾多次表达希望采取建设性步骤
以遏制涌入。

担心发生摩擦

此外，发言人声称，日本防区内
的犹太人口约占上海日本人口的
十分之一，这一事实导致人们担
心这两个社区之间会发生摩擦。
他补充说，鉴于上海尚未恢复正
常状态，且目前房屋严重短缺，
这是一项暂时采取的措施。

“目前，甚至对进入上海的日本
人数量也有限制，”发言人指出。

在回答提问时，发言人坚持认为，
这是由于当前情况而采取的紧急
措施，并且是根据犹太难民委员
会要求采取明确行动的请求而采
取的。

page_data.en:
23236

The spokesman pointed out that
although the matter of admission
of refugees to Shanghai was raised
several times before the Consular
Body, nothing had been done, and
as it was an acute question, the
Japanese Naval authorities had de-
cided to take the initiative in their
controlled area.
The Army spokesman stated that
areas west of Shanghai and those
coming under Army control were
open for residence of the Jewish
emigres.
The Navy spokesman pointed out
that the Consular Body had been
informed of the contemplated Jap-
anese action.
Not A Precedent
Upon being asked if a precedent
was established, the Japanese
could later restrict to other for-
eigners, including Britons and
Americans, the right of domicile
and doing business in Hongkew, the
spokesman replied that this was an
entirely different issue.
He stated that there was no re-
striction for Jewish emigrants pro-
ceeding to Tsingtao or Tientsin.

（批：Jo 9 1/4）
page_data.zh:
23236

发言人指出，虽然难民进入上海
的问题曾在领事团面前提起过几
次，但未采取任何行动，由于这
是一个紧迫的问题，日本海军当
局决定在其控制区域内采取主动。
陆军发言人表示，上海西部及陆
军控制的地区对犹太移民开放居
住。
海军发言人指出，已就日本拟采
取的行动通知了领事团。
并非先例
当被问及是否确立了先例，即日
本以后是否可以限制包括英国人
和美国人在内的其他外国人在虹
口居住和经商的权利时，发言人
回答说，这是一个完全不同的问
题。
他表示，前往青岛或天津的犹太
移民不受限制。

（批：Jo 9 1/4）

Special Branch,
June 3, 1939.

JEWISH REFUGEES.

The following statistics show the total
number of arrivals up to and including June 2, 1939 :-

Men....... 5,200
Women..... 3,800
Infants.... 1,000
TOTAL.....10,000

450 newcomers have been placed in jobs, etc.
permitting 800 persons in the shape of their wives and
families to become independent of any aid from the
Relief Organizations.

A further 400 refugees have been established in
various businesses in Shanghai, which has allowed another
1,200 persons to become independent of charitable assistance.

Thus, 2,000 persons, or 20% of the refugees, are
in a position where help from the local relief committees
is not needed.

Sir,

With reference to attached file, D.S.I. Gigarson and the undersigned have kept observation on the "Carso" Cafe at 1098 Broadway East, and made general enquiries regarding the alleged holding of political meetings by the Jewish refugees.

On the front door of the "Carso" Cafe there is an enamelled plate bearing the inscription "Clublokal das Makkabi" and refers to a general sports club formed by a number of refugees. The enamelled plate was put up at expense of the "Carso" management because of additional business accruing through. the club meetings being held there.

Information was received by D.S.I. Gigarson that a meeting was being held in the rear room of the "Carso" Cafe at 9 p.m. on April 27th. He attended and found about thirty-four Jewish refugees including four females between the ages of 18 to 35 years, present.

A male member of the party arose and made a speech in German the following being the gist of same noted by D.S.I. Gigarson.

The speaker made it known that Dr. Rosenberg, for some unknown reason, could not attend that evening. He went on to state that the "Makkabi" club was a Jewish sports club all over the world. That this local club was founded on February 1st 1939 and consists of about 200 members. He suggested that a greater number of members was required and that it did not matter whether they were Zionists or not as before everything everyone of us are Jews.

The club is endeavouring to become a Hongkew Branch of the Jewish Recreation Club of Shanghai and that he (the speaker)

Dc. (S.B).

在“Carso”咖啡馆的前门上有一块搪瓷牌，上面刻有“Clublokal das Makkabi”字样，指的是由一些难民组建的一个普通体育俱乐部。这块搪瓷牌是由“Carso”管理层出资安装的，因为俱乐部会议在此举行带来了额外的生意。

警佐 Gigarson 收到情报称，4月27日晚9点将在“Carso”咖啡馆的后屋举行会议。他到场后发现约有34名犹太难民在场，其中包括4名年龄在18至35岁之间的女性。

发言人表示，由于某些未知原因，Rosenberg 博士当晚无法出席。他接着说，“Makkabi”俱乐部是一个遍布全球的犹太人体育俱乐部。该本地俱乐部成立于1939年2月1日，拥有约200名会员。他建议需要更多的会员，并且无论他们是否是锡安主义者都无关紧要，因为最重要的是，我们都是犹太人。

Subject Central European Jews - Arrival in Shanghai
- alleged political meetings

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Crawford O.J

With reference to the contents of a paragraph appearing in a report dated March 15 (flagged) relating to meetings held by Central European Jews at the Cafe Corso, 1098 Broadway East, under the auspices of Drs. ROSENBERG, MOSSE and FREUND, information is now to hand which indicates that these gatherings are being conducted on political lines that appear to be inimical to the good of the Settlement.

It is learned that the three gentlemen mentioned above have been asked by the responsible officers of the local Jewish Refugee Committees to cease their activities as such run counter to the efforts of the Committees in caring for the new arrivals who are expressly forbidden to indulge in political matters of any kind. Drs. ROSENBERG and MOSSE have been informed by the Relief Committees that the refugees could well join the long established Shanghai Jewish Club in Moulmein Road if the joining of a Club is thought essential to their welfare, but that their (the doctors') attempts to cause discord between the refugees and Committees by establishing what is something akin to a political Club is entirely unnecessary and at variance with the spirit in which the Relief Committees are looking after the welfare of the refugees.

（左侧手写批注：）
I agree with Dr. S.P.R.
Licences be issued in regard to these semi-political meetings.

由 D.S. Pitts 撰写 由 C. Crawford O.J 转呈

关于3月15日报告（已标记）中一段涉及中欧犹太人在百老汇东路1098号 Corso 咖啡馆、在 ROSENBERG、MOSSE 和 FREUND 博士主持下举行集会的内容，现获情报显示，这些聚会的性质带有政治色彩，似乎不利于租界的利益。

据悉，当地犹太难民委员会的负责官员已要求上述三位绅士停止此类活动，因为这些活动违背了委员会照顾新来者的努力，而新来者被明确禁止参与任何形式的政治事务。救济委员会已告知 ROSENBERG 和 MOSSE 博士，如果认为加入俱乐部对他们的福祉至关重要，难民完全可以加入位于慕尔鸣路（Moulmein Road）历史悠久的上海犹太俱乐部，但是，他们（指两位博士）试图通过建立一个类似政治俱乐部的组织来在难民和委员会之间制造不和，这完全是没有必要的，也与救济委员会照顾难民福祉的精神相悖。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Miso. File No. 201/39.
Wayeide Station,
REPORT
Date May 19, 1939.
Subject Disembarkation of Passengers from M.V. Scharnhorst at Shanghai and
Hongkew Wharf.
Made by D.S.I. McCahey. Forwarded by Officer i/c.

Sir,
It is reported for information that the Norddeutscher
Lloyd M.V. "Scharnhorst" arrived in Shanghai and tied up at the
Shanghai and Hongkew Wharf at about 1 p.m. May 19th and that
the Chinese Maritime Customs Authorities allowed the disembarka-
tion of all foreign passengers with their baggage on the wharf.
However, Chinese passengers with their baggage were required
to proceed to the Customs Jetty by launch as has been the
practice for many months.
There were several hundred Jewish refugees, alleged to be
about six hundred, disembarked from this ship.
Chinese Customs Officers and Chinese members of the
River Police were also on duty on the wharf. The Commissioner
of Customs Mr. L.H. Lawford was also present on the wharf.

Yours obediently,
D. S. I.

D.D.C. "D".
D.C. (Special Branch).

先生，
谨此报告供参考：北德意志劳埃德公司（Norddeutscher
Lloyd）机动船“沙恩霍斯特”号（Scharnhorst）于5月19日下午1时左右抵达上海并停靠
在上海及虹口码头，中国海关当局允许所有外籍乘客
及其行李在码头上岸。然而，中国乘客及其行李需按
数月来的惯例，乘驳船前往海关栈桥。
据称约有六百名犹太难民从该船
下船。
中国海关官员和中国水上警察成员也在码头
执勤。海关税务司 L.H. Lawford 先生也出现在码头。

此致，
敬礼

D. S. I.

D.D.C. "D".

REPORT

S.4., Special Branch XXXXXX Station. File No.................... Date April 11th, 1942.

SUBJECT: The Present Functions of the "I.C" Committee.

After the outbreak of the Pacific War the offices
of the "International Committee for the Organization of
European Jewish Immigrants in China", which were located
in the Cathay Hotel, were closed as being part of the
Sassoon property. In the beginning of 1942 the military
administrators of the property charged Mr. B. Topaz, the
chairman of the Ashkenazi-Community in Shanghai, with
the task of auditing the Committee's books and making
the necessary preparations for a re-opening of the
office.

On March 16th, 1942, an office was opened on the
1st floor of the Sassoon House and the "Emigrant's
Thrift-Shop" at 55 Nanking Road also resumed operations,
both with a staff of 10 former employees under a new
secretary, Mr. Ohlmert, a friend of Mr. Topaz!. The
Committee is presently governed by a supervisory board
consisting of Messrs. Topaz, R.D. Abraham of D.E.J.
Abraham, 83 Peking Road, and Dr. Kardegg, the Chairman
of the "Community of Central European Jews (Juedische
Gemeinde)". These three in turn report to Mr. Inoye
of the Sassoon property administration and Mr. Shibata
of the Japanese Consulate-General.

Of the Committee's many functions the following
continue to exist:

1. The above mentioned "Thrift-Shop".
2. The "I.C. Nursery".
3. Support of the "Ort", a training school for
engineers, mechanics, carpenters, etc.
4. Collecting of loans, granted to refugees for
the establishment of enterprises, shops, etc.

主题：“I.C”委员会目前的职能。

太平洋战争爆发后，位于华懋饭店的“在华欧洲犹太移民组织国际委员会”办公室因属于沙逊产业的一部分而关闭。1942年初，该产业的军事管理人委托上海阿什肯纳兹社区主席 B. Topaz 先生审计委员会账目，并为重新开放办公室做必要准备。

1942年3月16日，在沙逊大厦一楼开设了一间办公室，南京路55号的“移民旧货店”也恢复运营，两者均由10名前雇员组成的工作人员在新任秘书 Ohlmert 先生（Topaz 先生的朋友）领导下工作。委员会目前由一个监事会管理，成员包括 Topaz 先生、北京路83号 D.E.J. Abraham 公司的 R.D. Abraham 先生，以及“中欧犹太人社区（Juedische Gemeinde）”主席 Kardegg 博士。这三人依次向沙逊产业管理处的 Inoye 先生和日本总领事馆的 Shibata 先生汇报。

委员会的众多职能中，以下职能继续存在：

1. 上述“旧货店”。
2. “I.C. 托儿所”。
3. 支持“Ort”，一所培训工程师、机械师、木匠等的学校。
4. 收回发放给难民用于建立企业、商店等的贷款。

5. Contributions to various charitable purposes,

According to Mr. Topaz, who was interviewed
with regard to the above, the Committee will continue
to carry out these functions on the basis of a
conservation of its capital, proceeds to go to charitable
purposes.

When questioned about the passports issued formerly
by the Committee and endorsed by the S.M.Police, Mr.
Topaz stated that they will have to be returned by
their holders. The possibility of issuing new passports
to Central European Jewish refugees similar to those,
issued by the Russian Emigrants Committee has already
been discussed.

With regard to the Committee's registers, which
contain records and photos of nearly 16,000 persons,
Mr. Topaz explained, that when no agreement could be
reached as to how to dispose of them, it was decided
that they should be left in his (Mr. Topaz's) personal
charge. Should the Police require any information,
contained in these records, Mr. Topaz would have to be
contacted. At present they are stored in a box room
on the first floor of the Sassoon House, near to the
Committee's office.

就上述事项接受问询的 Topaz 先生表示，委员会将在保全其资本的基础上继续履行这些职能，收益用于慈善目的。

当被问及以前由委员会签发并经上海公共租界工部局警务处背书的护照时，Topaz 先生表示，持有人必须将这些护照交回。关于向中欧犹太难民签发类似于俄罗斯移民委员会签发的新护照的可能性，已经进行了讨论。

关于委员会的登记册，其中包含近16,000人的记录和照片，Topaz 先生解释说，由于无法就如何处理这些登记册达成协议，决定将其留由他（Topaz 先生）个人保管。如果警方需要这些记录中包含的任何信息，必须联系 Topaz 先生。目前，它们存放在沙逊大厦一楼靠近委员会办公室的一间储藏室里。

The International Committee for the
Organization of European Immigrants
in China.

November 29th 1941.

Dear Sir,
With reference to my telephone conversation
with you yesterday morning, I hereby confirm that the
necessary measures which arise on our part due to the
new anti-jewish laws promulgated by the German Govern-
ment, whereby all Jews living abroad lose their nation-
ality, already exist, as you know, in part by our issuing
Documents of Identification in lieu of Passports which
are certified by you, Certificates of Character", endorse-
ments of Municipal Licences and so forth, and that these
services are immediately being extended to cover other
administrative work heretofore performed by the German
Consulate General and covering such documents as Birth-
and Death-Certificates and any other documents which in
the ordinary course of administrative work arise.

Such documents, e.g. Birth- and Death-Certi-
ficates, will be issued under our signature and seal,
and as indicated yesterday and approved by your good-
selves, endorsed by you in the same way as Documents of
Identification have been and are being endorsed.

I am very happy that foreseeing the present
developments, my organisation has created services which
can immediately take up the threads which are being se-
vered by the action of the German Government, and I sin-
cerely hope that by such services, the "I.C." will prove
useful to the Shanghai Municipal Police and the Adminis-
tration of the International Settlement in general.

I am, Dear Sir,

Your obedient servant,

Honorary Secretary.

T. Robertson Esquire,
Assistant Commissioner,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
Special Branch,
SHANGHAI.

1941年11月29日。

亲爱的先生：

参照昨日早晨与您的电话交谈，我特此确认，鉴于德国政府颁布新的反犹太法律，导致所有居住在海外的犹太人丧失国籍，我方为此采取的必要措施已经存在。如您所知，这部分措施包括由我方签发经贵方认证的身份证明文件以替代护照、品行证明书、市政许可证背书等；并且，这些服务正立即扩展至涵盖此前由德国总领事馆执行的其他行政工作，包括出生和死亡证明书以及在常规行政工作中产生的任何其他文件。

此类文件，例如出生和死亡证明书，将由我方签署并盖章，并按照昨日所示且经贵方批准的方式，由贵方以与身份证明文件相同的方式进行背书。

我很高兴我的组织预见到当前的事态发展，建立了能够立即接手因德国政府行动而中断的服务体系，并真诚希望透过这些服务，“I.C.”（国际委员会）能证明其对上海公共租界警务处及整个国际租界行政当局有所裨益。

此致，

您顺从的仆人，

THE INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE FOR THE
ORGANIZATION OF EUROPEAN IMMIGRANTS
IN CHINA

SHANGHAI, 29th November, 1941.

Dear Sir,

With reference to my telephone conversation
with you yesterday morning, I hereby confirm that the
necessary measures which arise on our part due to the
new anti-jewish laws promulgated by the German Govern-
ment, whereby all Jews living abroad lose their nation-
ality, already exist, as you know, in part by our issuing
Documents of Identification in lieu of Passports which
are certified by you, Certificates of Character, endorse-
ments of Municipal Licences and so forth, and that these
services are immediately being extended to cover other
administrative work heretofore performed by the German
Consulate General and covering such documents as Birth-
and Death-Certificates and any other documents which in
the ordinary course of administrative work arise.

Such documents, e.g. Birth- and Death-Certi-
ficates, will be issued under our signature and seal,
and as indicated yesterday and approved by your good-
selves, endorsed by you in the same way as Documents of
Identification have been and are being endorsed.

I am very happy that foreseeing the present
developments, my organisation has created services which
can immediately take up the threads which are being se-
vered by the action of the German Government, and I sin-
cerely hope that by such services, the "I.C." will prove
useful to the Shanghai Municipal Police and the Adminis-
tration of the International Settlement in general.

I am, Dear Sir,

Your obedient servant,

Hon. Secretary.

T. Robertson Esquire,
Assistant Commissioner,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
Special Branch,
SHANGHAI.

亲爱的先生：

参照昨日早晨与您的电话交谈，我特此确认，鉴于德国政府颁布新的反犹太法律，导致所有居住在海外的犹太人丧失国籍，我方为此采取的必要措施已经存在。如您所知，这部分措施包括由我方签发经贵方认证的身份证明文件以替代护照、品行证明书、市政许可证背书等；并且，这些服务正立即扩展至涵盖此前由德国总领事馆执行的其他行政工作，包括出生和死亡证明书以及在常规行政工作中产生的任何其他文件。

我很高兴我的组织预见到当前的事态发展，建立了能够立即接手因德国政府行动而中断的服务体系，并真诚希望透过这些服务，“I.C.”（国际委员会）能证明其对上海公共租界警务处及整个国际租界行政当局有所裨益。

此致，

Mr. Komor:

Re: My conversation with Vice-Consul Betz of the German
Consulate regarding denationalization.

This report was made by "Transocean" and is said to be absolutely
correct for "Full-Jews" who live abroad.

Mr. Betz told me, when I asked him why the German Consulate-General
had not even today, 8 days after the report was published in the
"Ostasiatischer Lloyd", made an official declaration regarding it,
that the papers were of course working faster than the Courier.
The letter was daily expected by the German Consulate General.
Should no message arrive up to the 10th of December, the German
Consulate General would cable to Berlin.

"You surely can imagine", Mr. Betz said to me, "that Germany today
has far more important things to do, we have to wage a huge war in
the East; in the West it would be different, the official
authorities today work only with 40% of their staff as every able man
has joined the army."

Mr. Betz regretted to be unable to tell me any more than the
"Transocean" report said.

"We regard the matter as being frozen up, but as this Agency is the
official German one, you can tell your people that the report about
the denationalization of the Jews living abroad is correct. But
before we make a general alteration, it would be better to wait
for the execution orders."

Concerning the 14 Passports retained by the Consulate, Mr. Betz is
going to recommend my proposition. Should the Passports actually
be confiscated by the Reich, the Passports shall be annulled by
the German Consulate General and will be returned to me for
distribution to the owners of the respective Passports.

The conference was held in a very friendly and often private
atmosphere.

sd. Willy Baruch
Shanghai, December 5, 1941

（印：INTS' ORGAM. SHANGHAI）

Komor 先生：

事由：我与德国领事馆副领事 Betz 关于剥夺国籍问题的谈话。

本报告由“Transocean”（跨洋通讯社）发布，据称对于居住在国外的“纯种犹太人”绝对准确。

当我询问 Betz 先生，为何在《东亚劳埃德日报》（Ostasiatischer Lloyd）刊登该报道8天后的今天，德国总领事馆仍未就此发表官方声明时，他告诉我，报纸的工作速度当然比信使快。德国总领事馆每天都在等待信件。如果到12月10日还没有消息到达，德国总领事馆将向柏林发电报。

“您肯定可以想象”，Betz 先生对我说，“德国今天有更重要的事情要做，我们必须在东方进行一场大规模战争；如果在西方，情况就会不同，目前的官方机构只有40%的人员在工作，因为每个有能力的人都参军了。”

Betz 先生遗憾地表示，除了“Transocean”报道的内容外，他无法告诉我更多信息。

“我们将此事视为冻结状态，但由于本机构是德国官方机构，您可以告诉您的人们，关于剥夺居住在海外的犹太人国籍的报道是正确的。但在我们做出普遍变更之前，最好等待执行命令。”

关于领事馆扣留的14本护照，Betz 先生打算推荐我的提议。如果这些护照确实被帝国没收，德国总领事馆将注销这些护照，并将其退还给我，以便分发给各护照持有人。

会议在非常友好且时常私下的气氛中进行。

签署：Willy Baruch
上海，1941年12月5日

（印：INTS' ORGAM. SHANGHAI）
D.C. (Covers)
诽谤
（印：POLICE 1941 SOCIAL BRANCH）

Special Branch,
July 6, 1939.

Commissioner.

Sir,

Rumours of unscrupulous tactics on the
part of Mr. Komor in his I.C. work are current
at the moment and it is possible that those
responsible will break into press in the near
future. I think Mr. Hayim has something to do
with it as the feeling between him and Komor is
reported to be anything but friendly.

Reference attached minutes and Mr. Komor's
request for strengthening of the present Committee,
I am of opinion that the question should be shelved
for the time being. I suggested to Mr. Komor that
it was unfortunate that prominent local members of
the Jewish community could not work together in
relief matters. He was more or less non-committal
in his reply, merely venturing the statement that
he was out for immediate relief and had little
interest in projects which would take a year or two
to materialize.

目前流传着关于科莫尔先生 (Mr. Komor) 在其国际委员会 (I.C.) 工作中采取不择手段策略的谣言，相关责任人有可能在不久的将来诉诸报端。我认为海姆先生 (Mr. Hayim) 与此事有关，因为据称他与科莫尔之间的关系绝非友好。

参照所附会议记录及科莫尔先生关于加强现有委员会的请求，我认为该问题应暂时搁置。我曾向科莫尔先生建议，犹太社区的当地知名人士无法在救济事务上合作，实为憾事。他的回答模棱两可，仅表示他致力于即时救济，对那些需要一两年才能见效的项目兴趣不大。

Special Branch.
July 6, 1939.

Commissioner.

Sir,

Rumours of unscrupulous tactics on the
part of Mr. Komor in his I.C. work are current
at the moment and it is possible that those
responsible will break into press in the near
future. I think Mr. Hayim has something to do
with it as the feeling between him and Komor is
reported to be anything but friendly.

Reference attached minutes and Mr. Komor's
request for strengthening of the present Committee,
I am of opinion that the question should be shelved
for the time being. I suggested to Mr. Komor that
it was unfortunate that prominent local members of
the Jewish community could not work together in
relief matters. He was more or less non-committal
in his reply, merely venturing the statement that
he was out for immediate relief and had little
interest in projects which would take a year or two
to materialize.

(Sd) Thos. Robertson
D.C. (Special Branch)

page_data.en:
The fourth meeting in connection with the problems
attending the arrival in Shanghai of Central European Jews
was held in the Medical Library, Public Health Department,
at 3 p.m., June 22, 1939.

Present
Mr. Paul KOMOR - "I.C." Relief Fund.
Dr. LUCKE }
Chief Inspector SELF } - Public Health Department.
Mr. T. ROBERTSON }
Detective Sergeant PITTS } - Police Department.

The minutes of the previous meeting having been
circulated and read, and no dissension having been voiced
at the contents, they were approved and confirmed.

At the outset, Mr. KOMOR, in discussing various
matters of general interest relating to the problem in hand,
suggested that for the purpose of strengthening the present
Committee and to allow it to make public its findings, it
should be given some sort of official status and that its
chairman should be a Municipal Councillor. Mr. KOMOR requested
that this suggestion be given the serious consideration of the
proper quarters.

PUBLIC HEALTH DEPARTMENT

It having been announced by Mr. SELF that the
premises at Choufoong Road, temporarily utilized as a
hospital in combatting the scarlet-fever epidemic, having
been closed, the speaker pointed out that immediate steps
should be taken by the responsible refugee committees to
find other suitable accommodation where communicable diseases
could be treated without delay.
page_data.zh:
关于中欧犹太人抵达上海所伴随问题的第四次会议，于1939年6月22日下午3时在公共卫生处医学图书馆举行。

出席人员
保罗·科莫尔先生 (Mr. Paul KOMOR) - “I.C.” 救济基金。
卢克博士 (Dr. LUCKE) }
塞尔夫总督察 (Chief Inspector SELF) } - 公共卫生处。
T. 罗伯逊先生 (Mr. T. ROBERTSON) }
警长皮茨 (Detective Sergeant PITTS) } - 警务处。

上次会议的纪要已传阅并宣读，鉴于对内容无异议，予以批准和确认。

会议伊始，科莫尔先生在讨论与手头问题相关的各种普遍关注事项时建议，为了加强现有委员会并使其能够公开其调查结果，应赋予其某种官方地位，且其主席应由一名工部局董事担任。科莫尔先生请求有关部门认真考虑此建议。

公共卫生处

鉴于塞尔夫先生宣布，周丰路（音译）上临时用作抗击猩红热流行病医院的场所已关闭，发言人指出，负责的难民委员会应立即采取措施，寻找其他合适的场所，以便毫不延误地治疗传染病。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

In this connection, Dr. LUCKE stated that it, too,
would be preferable if arrangements could also be made for
the reception of maternity and lunacy cases.

The P.H.D. representatives and Mr. KOMOR then
discussed at length the possibility of the constructing of
a new hospital for the refugees. Mr. KOMOR intimated that
Sir Elly KADOORIE had promised sometime ago to donate
$500,000 for the erection of a hospital of 50 beds but that
the matter was still in abeyance.

Mr. KOMOR then stated that he had made an appeal
through the press for $50,000 to enlarge the present premises
at Whashing Road, now being used as a general hospital. He
also mentioned that he had made an application to the S.M.C.
for a grant-in-aid in respect of the Whashing Road Hospital
and that in the event of any sum being granted, the Council
would automatically recognise the existence of the hospital
as being a public necessity.

Upon being asked whether the Health Department
could effectively help to eradicate the mosquito nuisance
in the Refugee Camps of the Northern Area, Mr. SELF stated
that all possible steps were being and would be taken to
stamp out this menace, but that the S.M.C. would not provide
wirenetting for the Camps.

Mr. SELF expressed his pleasure at the fact that
sanitation arrangements in all camps were satisfactory,
while he mentioned that simple health lectures would continue
to be given in the camps by persons nominated by the Refugee
Committees at regular intervals.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

对此，卢克博士表示，如果也能安排接收产妇和精神病患者病例，那就更好了。

随后，公共卫生处代表与科莫尔先生详细讨论了为难民建造新医院的可能性。科莫尔先生透露，埃利·嘉道理爵士 (Sir Elly KADOORIE) 曾在不久前承诺捐赠50万美元用于建造一所拥有50张床位的医院，但该事项仍处于搁置状态。

科莫尔先生接着表示，他已通过媒体呼吁筹集5万美元，以扩建目前作为综合医院使用的华盛路（音译）现有场所。他还提到，他已向工部局申请对华盛路医院提供补助，并且如果获批任何款项，工部局将自动承认该医院的存在是公共必需品。

当被问及卫生处能否有效帮助消除北区难民营的蚊虫滋扰时，塞尔夫先生表示，正在并将采取一切可能的措施来消除此危害，但工部局不会为难民营提供铁丝网。

塞尔夫先生对所有难民营的卫生安排令人满意表示欣慰，同时他提到，将由难民委员会提名的人员定期在难民营举办简单的健康讲座。

page_data.en:
- 3 -
POLICE DEPARTMENT
Mr. KOMOR, in reply to a question put by
Mr. ROBERTSON, stated that over 7,000 refugees had
registered with the "I.C." Relief Fund and that their
full particulars were now on record for Police
inspection at any time.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -
警务处
科莫尔先生在回答罗伯逊先生提出的问题时表示，已有超过7,000名难民在“I.C.”救济基金登记，他们的详细资料现已存档，随时可供警方查阅。

SELF 先生对所有难民营的卫生安排令人满意表示欣慰，同时他提到，由难民委员会提名的人员将继续定期在难民营内举办简单的健康讲座。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

Mr. ROBERTSON, stated that over 7,000 refugees had
registered with the "I.C." Relief Fund and that their
full particulars were now on record for Police
inspection at any time.

page_data.en:
The third meeting in connection with the problems
attending the arrival in Shanghai of Central European
Jews was held in the Medical Library, Public Health
Department, at 3 p.m. May 25, 1939.

Present :-

Mr. PAUL KOMOR - "I.C." Relief Fund.

Dr. LUCKE
Chief Inspector SELF } - Public Health Department.

Chief Detective-
Inspector ROSS
Detective-Sergeant
PITTS } - Police Department.

The minutes of the last meeting held on May 11,
1939 were read but objection was voiced by the Health
Department representatives to that portion of the last
sentence of the first paragraph under the heading "Public
Health Department," reading "....... upon receipt of
which ....... the question of payment." It was
therefore decided that the paragraph in question should
be amended to conclude "....... debiting the said
Committee with the appropriate amount." The remainder
of the minutes were approved and confirmed.

PUBLIC HEALTH DEPARTMENT

Chaoufoong Road Hospital

In discussing the temporary hospital located at
Chaoufoong Road, Mr. KOMOR stated that a proposal had
been made to the effect that the emergency nature of this
hospital be changed to permit it to operate on a proper
and permanent basis, and that the school situated on the
site be transferred to the Kinchow Road Camp. Before
any steps could be taken in this direction, however, the
approval of the London Mission, owners of the property,
page_data.zh:
关于中欧犹太人抵达上海所伴随问题的第三次会议，于 1939 年 5 月 25 日下午 3 时在公共卫生处医学图书馆举行。

出席人员：

PAUL KOMOR 先生 - “国际委员会”（"I.C."）救济基金。

LUCKE 博士
SELF 总督察 } - 公共卫生处。

首席侦探
督察 ROSS
侦探警长
PITTS } - 警务处。

宣读了 1939 年 5 月 11 日举行的上次会议的纪要，但公共卫生处代表对标题为“公共卫生处”项下第一段最后一句的部分内容提出异议，该部分内容为：“....... 收到后 ....... 付款问题。”因此决定将该段修改为以“....... 向该委员会记入相应金额”结尾。纪要的其余部分获得批准并确认。

公共卫生处

兆丰路医院

在讨论位于兆丰路（Chaoufoong Road）的临时医院时，KOMOR 先生表示，已提出一项提议，旨在改变该医院的紧急性质，使其能够以正规和永久性的基础运作，并将位于该址的学校迁至荆州路（Kinchow Road）难民营。然而，在朝此方向采取任何步骤之前，首先需要得到物业所有者伦敦会（London Mission）的批准，

page_data.en:
- 2 -

would be first required. The speaker also mentioned
that in the event of the new measures being approved and
eventually taking effect, sufficient accommodation would
exist in the hospital for 300 beds.

In commenting on these remarks, Dr. LUCKE pointed
out that the responsible Refugee Committees would, in
the future, be well advised to reserve at least 100
beds for emergency and infectious cases.

Scarlet Fever Epidemic

In order to impress upon the Committee the
urgency of establishing the hospital in Chaoufoong Road,
Mr. SELF read out figures relating to the scarlet fever
epidemic, details of which are :-

May 4 ......... 32 cases
May 5 ......... increase of 32 cases
May 6 ......... increase of 21 cases
May 7 ......... increase of 21 cases,

after which date the number of cases steadily mounted
until May 22, when 124 patients were being treated. On
the first day of the outbreak, 32 cases of communicable
disease having been recorded, it was quite impossible
to find suitable accommodation in S.M.C. hospitals.
The matter was immediately discussed with the Commissioner
of Public Health who came to the decision that the
premises at Chaoufoong Road must be utilized as a
hospital.

In view of these measures, Mr. SELF stated, he
was glad to report that since May 11 only 9 further
cases had been notified, whereas had these steps not
been taken, this epidemic might have become completely
out of control.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

发言人还提到，如果新措施获得批准并最终生效，该医院将有足够的空间容纳 300 张床位。

在对这些言论进行评论时，LUCKE 博士指出，建议负责的难民委员会今后至少预留 100 张床位，用于急诊和传染病病例。

猩红热流行病

为了让委员会认识到在兆丰路建立医院的紧迫性，SELF 先生宣读了有关猩红热流行病的数据，详情如下：

5 月 4 日 ......... 32 例
5 月 5 日 ......... 增加 32 例
5 月 6 日 ......... 增加 21 例
5 月 7 日 ......... 增加 21 例，

此后病例数稳步上升，直到 5 月 22 日，接受治疗的患者达到 124 人。在疫情爆发的第一天，记录了 32 例传染病病例，在工部局医院中完全无法找到合适的收容场所。此事立即与公共卫生处处长进行了讨论，后者决定必须利用兆丰路的院舍作为医院。

SELF 先生表示，鉴于这些措施，他很高兴地报告说，自 5 月 11 日以来仅通报了 9 例新增病例，而如果不采取这些步骤，这场流行病可能会完全失控。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

General Management of Camps

Mr. SELF reported on the excellent condition of
the General Hospital at Whasing Road but stated there
was still room for considerable improvement in regard
to cleanliness in the Communicable Diseases Hospital
at Chaoufoong Road. Mr. KOMOR noted these remarks
which, he said, would be attended to.

Refugee Schools

Mention was made by the Health Department
representatives that the Kinchow Road Schools had been
cleared of all furniture by the Public Works Department
and would now be utilized as combined refugee camps and
schools.

Dr. LUCKE requested that the local Jewish Refugee
Committees do all in their power to have the schools
opened as quickly as possible in order to permit the
many Jewish children to attend and thus minimize their
opportunities of contracting sickness by continually
playing in the streets. Mr. KOMOR promised that this
matter would receive early attention.

POLICE DEPARTMENT

Posters

In reply to a question put by C.D.I. ROSS,
Mr. KOMOR stated that the reaction from the posting of
notices urging newcomers to register with the "I.C."
Relief Fund Committee, had not been as successful as
anticipated, but in order to press home the advantage
that the notices had undoubtedly brought, he was having
another poster printed and displayed in prominent spots
which would state that those refugees who had arrived
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

难民营的总体管理

SELF 先生报告了华盛路（Whasing Road）综合医院的良好状况，但指出兆丰路传染病医院的清洁程度仍有相当大的改进空间。KOMOR 先生注意到了这些意见，并表示将予以处理。

难民学校

公共卫生处代表提到，工务局已清空荆州路（Kinchow Road）学校的所有家具，该校舍现在将被用作难民营和学校的混合设施。

LUCKE 博士请求当地犹太难民委员会尽其所能尽快开放学校，以便让众多犹太儿童入学，从而通过减少他们在街道上持续玩耍的机会，最大限度地降低他们感染疾病的风险。KOMOR 先生承诺将尽早关注此事。

警务处

海报

在回答首席侦探督察 ROSS 提出的问题时，KOMOR 先生表示，张贴敦促新来者向“国际委员会”（"I.C."）救济基金委员会登记的通知后，反响不如预期成功，但为了强调这些通知无疑带来的好处，他正在印制另一张海报，并在显眼位置展示，声明那些于

page_data.en:
- 4 -

in Shanghai more than three months ago must register
all personal details with his Committee not later than
June 21, 1939, failure to comply with these instructions
to definitely entail the withdrawal of all future
financial aid. C.D.I. ROSS remarked that, from a
Police viewpoint, the arrangement was most satisfactory.

----------
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

三个月前抵达上海的难民，必须在 1939 年 6 月 21 日之前向其委员会登记所有个人详细信息，不遵守这些指示将明确导致取消所有未来的经济援助。首席侦探督察 ROSS 评论说，从警方角度来看，这一安排非常令人满意。

page_data.en:
The Second Meeting in connection with the problems
attending the arrival in Shanghai of Central European
Jews was held in the Medical Library, Public Health
Department, at 3 p.m., May 11, 1939.

Present :-

Mr. KOMOR - "I.C." Relief Fund.

Dr. LUCKE, }
Chief Inspector SELF } Public Health Department.

Chief Detective }
Inspector ROSS } Police Department.
Detective Sergeant PITTS }

It being deemed unnecessary to appoint a
chairman at this stage of the proceedings, the business
in hand was dealt with as expeditiously as possible,
with D.S. PITTS recording the points raised and discussed.

PUBLIC HEALTH DEPARTMENT

Dr. LUCKE drew Mr. KOMOR's attention to the
fact that several thousand refugees had been inoculated
against cholera and that a similar number of inoculation
Certificate Cards had been issued by the S.M.C. to the
"I.C." Relief Fund Committee. Since each card cost
50 cents, the S.M.C. intended debiting the said Committee
with the appropriate amount, upon receipt of which the
Committee could discuss with the Council the question
of payment.

Disinfection Services

It was pointed out by Mr. SELF that disinfection
services operated by the Council in respect of communicable
diseases were carried out free of charge, but since many of
the refugees were not ratepayers, it had been decided by
the Council that the "I.C." Relief Fund Committee should
page_data.zh:
关于中欧犹太人抵达上海所伴随问题的第二次会议于1939年5月11日下午3时在公共卫生处医学图书馆举行。

出席者：

科莫尔（KOMOR）先生 - “国际委员会”救济基金。

拉克博士（Dr. LUCKE），}
塞尔夫（SELF）总巡官 } 公共卫生处。

首席侦探 }
罗斯（ROSS）巡官 } 警务处。
皮茨（PITTS）侦探警长 }

鉴于在现阶段认为无需任命主席，故尽可能迅速处理手头事务，由 D.S. 皮茨记录提出和讨论的要点。

公共卫生处

拉克博士提请科莫尔先生注意，已有数千名难民接种了霍乱疫苗，且工部局已向“国际委员会”救济基金委员会签发了同等数量的接种证书卡。由于每张卡片成本为5角，工部局打算在向该委员会收到相应款项后向其记帐，届时该委员会可与工部局商讨付款事宜。

消毒服务

塞尔夫先生指出，工部局针对传染病开展的消毒服务是免费进行的，但由于许多难民并非纳税人，工部局已决定要求“国际委员会”救济基金委员会

page_data.en:
- 2 -
be asked to pay for such services at reduced rates.
Mr. KOMOR accordingly took due note of these remarks
and stated that the question of payment would be one
upon which he would communicate with the proper
quarters in the Council.

Ambulance Service
Mention was made by Mr. SELF of the fact that
charges for the use of the Shanghai Fire Brigade
Ambulance used in removing to their hospital refugees
suffering from scarlet fever were debited the Public
Health Department. Mr. KOMOR was advised that his
Committee would be debited with these expenses in
due course.

Jewish Refugee Isolation Hospital in Chaoufoong Road -
Scarlet Fever Epidemic
The recent scarlet fever epidemic among the
refugees and the necessity for isolating patients
suffering therefrom were discussed at length.
Mr. KOMOR stated that the disease had fallen like a
bombshell with no previous warning and that measures
had been immediately enforced to prevent a greater
spread and that when the epidemic assumed major
proportions, premises at Medhurst College in Chaoufoong
Road had been brought into use as an Isolation Hospital
at the suggestion of the Public Health Department.
Mr. SELF stated that it would be preferable if
arrangements could be made for this Hospital to be kept
open, at least, throughout the summer, as the building
itself was far better than the S.M.C. Isolation Hospital
approximately
and would accommodate/300 patients. This point was
corroborated by Dr. LUCKE who said that 113 cases were
being tended in the Hospital at the present time.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -
以优惠费率支付此类服务费用。
科莫尔先生 accordingly  duly noted these remarks and stated that the question of payment would be one upon which he would communicate with the proper quarters in the Council.
（译者注：此处原文为英文，按语境翻译如下：）
科莫尔先生 accordingly  duly noted these remarks and stated that the question of payment would be one upon which he would communicate with the proper quarters in the Council.
科莫尔先生对此言论予以充分关注，并表示付款问题他将与工部局有关部门进行沟通。

救护车服务
塞尔夫先生提到，用于将患猩红热的难民运送至医院的上海救火会救护车的使用费，已记入公共卫生处帐下。已告知科莫尔先生，这些费用将在适当时候记入其委员会帐下。

兆丰路犹太难民隔离医院 - 猩红热流行
最近难民中爆发的猩红热疫情以及隔离患者的必要性得到了详细讨论。
科莫尔先生表示，该疾病如炸弹般突然降临，毫无预兆，已立即采取措施防止进一步扩散；当疫情规模扩大时，根据公共卫生处的建议，位于兆丰路的麦赫斯特学院（Medhurst College）房舍已被用作隔离医院。
塞尔夫先生表示，如果能安排该医院至少在整个夏季保持开放，那将更为可取，因为该建筑本身远优于工部局的隔离医院，大约可容纳300名患者。这一点得到了拉克博士的证实，他说目前医院正在收治113例病例。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

It was stressed by Dr. LUCKE, after he had been
informed that the number of refugees in Shanghai at the
end of June would possibly amount to 11,000 or more,
that the crowded and unsanitary surroundings in which
the refugees were finding themselves, might lead to a
further spread of disease and that in the event of
accommodation in the Chaoufoong Road building being
insufficient to cope with various summer infectious
diseases, temporary measures should be adopted by the
erection of matsheds or other similar constructions.
In making these remarks, the speaker intimated that the
contingency of a cholera epidemic taking hold of the
refugees during the coming months was one that must not
for one moment be neglected and that measures on the
lines mentioned higher should be enforced to prevent
any serious spread.

That the Japanese were interesting themselves in
the refugee problem was manifest, said Mr. KOMOR, two
Japanese in uniform - presumably naval officers - having
visited and inspected the hospital on May 10.

Simple Health Measures

Mr. SELF pointed out that the newcomers would be
well advised to pay as much attention as possible to simple
health measures and he asked Mr. KOMOR to request the
refugees to purchase, for instance, ice, ice-cream,
mineral-waters, etc., from only reputable licensed
establishments. Mr. KOMOR replied that simple and
essential health rules had already been drawn up for
distribution among the refugees.

Dr. LUCKE then requested that Chinese hawkers be
strictly forbidden to enter any refugee camp in order to
minimize the spread of infection and disease through the
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

拉克博士在获悉6月底上海的难民人数可能达到11,000人或更多后强调，难民所处的拥挤和不卫生的环境可能导致疾病进一步传播；如果兆丰路建筑的住宿设施不足以应对各种夏季传染病，应采取搭建席棚或其他类似建筑的临时措施。在发表这些言论时，发言者暗示，未来几个月难民中爆发霍乱疫情的可能性绝不可忽视，必须执行上述措施以防止任何严重扩散。

科莫尔先生说，日本人显然对难民问题感兴趣，两名身穿制服的日本人——推测为海军军官——曾于5月10日参观并视察了该医院。

简单的卫生措施

塞尔夫先生指出，新来者最好尽可能注意简单的卫生措施，他请科莫尔先生要求难民仅从信誉良好的持牌场所购买冰块、冰淇淋、矿泉水等。科莫尔先生回答说，简单且必要的卫生规则已经制定完毕，正分发给难民。

随后，拉克博士请求严格禁止中国小贩进入任何难民营，以最大限度地减少因其兜售食品的不卫生状况而导致的感染和疾病传播。

page_data.en:
- 4 -

unhygienic condition of foodstuffs peddled by them.
He also asked that arrangements be made to have
policemen placed at the gates of such camps to prevent
the ingress of hawkers.

POLICE DEPARTMENT

Reference was made to the fact that the notices
requiring all newcomers to register with the Jewish
Relief Committees had been drawn up and posted in spots
frequented by the newcomers. Mr. KOMOR was asked by
C.D.I. ROSS to note, during the coming weeks, whether
any marked increase in registrations was recorded.

Mr. KOMOR then asked whether he could hold known
or suspected criminal elements in his office until the
arrival of the Police for purposes of questioning.
He was assured he could.

In order to minimize the chances of bad elements
being enlisted in the S.M.P. (Specials) and the S.V.C.,
Mr. KOMOR requested that details of all applications
for enrolment be unofficially passed to him before
approval, so that he might be given the opportunity of
investigating applicants' characters and antecedents.
He remarked that the Japanese authorities had been
heard to state that refugee volunteers would not be
permitted to reside north of the Soochow Creek.

The question of endorsing travel documents to
allow refugees to enter Shanghai from Germany was
examined by C.D.I. ROSS, who explained that the Berlin
Police demanded such endorsements from the Municipal
Police before permitting families to join their relatives
already arrived in Shanghai. Mr. KOMOR stated he did
not know why such endorsements were needed and since
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

他还要求安排警察驻守此类营地门口，以防止小贩进入。

警务处

会上提及，要求所有新来者向犹太救济委员会登记的通告已起草并张贴在新来者常去的地方。首席侦探巡官罗斯请科莫尔先生在未来几周内注意，登记人数是否有显著增加。

随后，科莫尔先生询问，为了便于警方讯问，他是否可以在其办公室扣留已知或涉嫌犯罪的人员，直到警方到达。他得到保证可以这样做。

为了最大限度地减少不良分子混入上海公共租界工部局警务处（特别警察）和上海义勇队，科莫尔先生请求在批准之前，非正式地将所有入伍申请的详细信息转交给他，以便他有机会调查申请人的品行和背景。他评论说，据闻日本当局曾表示，不允许难民志愿者居住在苏州河以北。

首席侦探巡官罗斯审查了为允许难民从德国进入上海而在旅行证件上加签的问题，他解释说，柏林警方要求在允许家属加入已抵达上海的亲属之前，必须由公共租界警务处在证件上加签。科莫尔先生表示，他不知道为何需要此类加签，而且既然

page_data.en:
- 5 -
they were only required for those travelling via Siberia,
this was a matter on which the official views of the
local German Consular Authorities might well be sought
by the Police.
The meeting terminated at 4.25 p.m. after
Mr. KOMOR had declared that, as far as he could see,
there was little chance of Shanghai successfully
absorbing the influx of newcomers for the next decade.
The majority of them were professional people and not
artisans and having no capital to commence business
in an already saturated market, were handicapped from
the start.
page_data.zh:
- 5 -
这仅适用于经西伯利亚旅行的人，那么警方可就此事项征求当地德国领事当局的官方意见。
会议于下午4时25分结束，此前科莫尔先生宣称，就他所见，上海在未来十年内成功吸收新来者涌入的机会渺茫。他们大多数是专业人士而非工匠，且在已经饱和的市场中没有资本开始经商，从一开始就处于不利地位。

Subject Central European Jews - Preliminary Committee Meeting

Made by. D. S. Pitts Forwarded by. C. Crawford. S.I.

In connection with recent correspondence
between the Commissioner of Police and the Secretary
of the Shanghai Municipal Council on topics relating
to the arrival in Shanghai of Central European Jews,
a preliminary meeting was held at 3.15 p.m., April 27,
1939 in the Medical Library, Public Health Department,
the following persons attending :-
Mr. P. KOMOR,
Chief Inspector SELF, Public Health Department,
Chief Detective Inspector ROSS, Police Department,
Detective-Sergeant PITTS, Police Department.
The meeting was convened for the frank
exchange of views of those present on problems
affecting the new-comers and to devise ways and
means that would enable :-
(1) The Police to exercise a greater control over
the movements and activities of the immigrants
than hitherto found possible with the primary
object of preventing crime, and
(2) The Public Health Department to prevent the
outbreak of epidemics among the new arrivals
by the application of simple prophylactic
measures.
The contents of recently submitted Special
Branch reports covering the various phases of the
Jewish Refugee problem being known to the Police and
Health Department representatives, it was not deemed

事由 中欧犹太人 - 委员会预备会议

制作人. D. S. 皮茨 (Pitts) 转呈人. C. 克劳福德 (Crawford). S.I.

鉴于警务处处长与上海公共租界工部局秘书之间最近就中欧犹太人抵达上海相关议题进行的通信，于1939年4月27日下午3时15分在公共卫生处医学图书馆举行了一次预备会议，出席人员如下：
P. 科莫尔 (P. KOMOR) 先生，
公共卫生处首席督察 SELF，
警务处首席侦探督察 ROSS，
警务处侦探警佐 PITTS。
召开会议旨在让与会者坦率交流关于影响新来者的问题的看法，并制定方法和手段，以便：
(1) 警方能够比以往更有效地控制移民的行动和活动，主要目的是预防犯罪，以及
(2) 公共卫生处能够通过实施简单的预防措施，防止新来者中爆发流行病。
由于警方和卫生处代表已知悉最近提交的涵盖犹太难民问题各个阶段的特别处报告的内容，因此认为

TRANSLATION FROM GERMAN

NOTICE
------

At an examination of our registration cards the
attention of the local Police authorities was drawn
to the fact there were no photographs (of holders)
on some of the cards and that only meagre particulars
of applicants were entered. On the other hand it
was also ascertained that no identification cards were
attached to such registration cards. The Police
suggested that care should be taken to have all
registration cards, without exception, filled in in
the fullest possible manner, that photographs be
attached to each registration card and that each
immigrant be issued with an identification card.

Cases where either photographs or identification
cards are absent will be treated with a certain amount
of suspicion as, in the opinion of the Police, the
persons concerned may have good reasons for avoiding
registration.

An earnest request is therefore again made that
every newcomer obtain an 'identification card for which
purpose, as is well known, two copies of photographs
are required. Those failing to comply with these
conditions cannot, in the case of necessity, rely on
future support and assistance from the Relief Committee.

SIGNED: P. KOMOR.

德文译文

通知
------

在检查我们的登记卡时，当地警方当局注意到，部分卡片上没有（持有人的）照片，且申请人的详细信息填写得非常简略。另一方面，还查明此类登记卡未附有身份证明卡。警方建议，应注意确保所有登记卡毫无例外地尽可能完整地填写，每份登记卡均附上照片，并向每位移民签发一张身份证明卡。

对于缺少照片或身份证明卡的情况，将带有一定程度的怀疑进行处理，因为警方认为，相关人员可能有充分理由避免登记。

因此再次恳切要求每位新来者获取一张“身份证明卡”，为此目的，众所周知需要两张照片。凡未能遵守这些条件者，在必要时，将无法指望从救济委员会获得未来的支持和援助。

签署：P. 科莫尔 (P. KOMOR)。

BEKANNTMACHUNG

Bei einer Überprüfung unserer Kartotheken ist es der
hiesigen Polizeiverwaltung aufgefallen, daß bei man-
chen Karten die Fotografien fehlen und die Einzelhei-
ten nur sehr dürftig ausgefüllt sind, andererseits wurde
auch festgestellt, daß bei solchen Karten auch die Emi-
granten - Legitimationskarten fehlen. Die Polizei legte
uns nahe, dafür Sorge zu tragen, daß ausnahmslos sämtliche
Meldekarten ohne Lücken möglichst vollständig ausgefüllt
werden und daß die Fotografien beigestellt werden, ferner
dass jeder Emigrant eine Legitimation erhält. Solche Fälle,
bei denen die Fotografien oder die Legitimationskarte feh-
len, werden mit Mißtrauen betrachtet, denn nach Meinung der
Polizei hat der Betreffende einen Grund diesen Anforderungen
nicht nachzukommen. X
Es wird daher nochmals dringend gebeten, daß Legitimations-
karten eingeholt werden, wozu bekanntlich zwei Fotografien
notwendig sind. Wer dieser Anforderung nicht nachkommt, kann
später im Notwendigkeitsfall auf die Unterstützung oder den
Beistand des Committees bei den Behörden nicht rechnen.

PAUL KORNER
Secretary & Treasurer

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.I, Special Branch Station, Z.
REPORT
Date June 29, 1939.
Subject Central European Jews - articles exploiting newcomers'
experiences published in local press
Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by [Signature]

With reference to the attached correspondence
from Mr. Paul KOMOR, Hon. Secretary of the "I.C.
Relief Committee," in connection with articles
appearing in the "Hwa Pao" of June 13, and in
"The China Weekly Review" of February 4 and June 10,
the view is expressed by the D.C. (Special Branch)
that no good purpose would be served by this office
in adopting measures to curtail the publication of
articles giving details of the past experiences of
newly arrived Jewish refugees. Any such line
of action might have the opposite result of the
effect desired and might stimulate the local reading
public's interest for further similar stories from
new arrivals.

Once the arrival of refugees in Shanghai has
assumed an aspect of lesser importance, it is
thought that the local press will treat the problem
with a corresponding lack of interest and cease to
publish relevant articles.

The views of the D.C. (Special Branch) have been
communicated to Mr. KOMOR, who has expressed his
satisfaction with the manner in which the contents
of his letter were received.

Ja Pitts
D. S.
D.C. (Special Branch)

呈报人：D.S. Pitts 转呈人：[签名]

关于附上的“国际救济委员会”（I.C. Relief Committee）荣誉秘书 Paul KOMOR 先生的来信，该信涉及6月13日《华报》以及2月4日和6月10日《密勒氏评论报》（The China Weekly Review）上刊登的文章，特务科副督察长（D.C. (Special Branch)）认为，本处若采取措施限制刊登详述新抵达犹太难民过往经历的文章，并不会带来任何益处。任何此类行动可能会产生与预期效果相反的结果，并可能激起本地读者公众对新来者更多类似故事的兴趣。

一旦难民抵达上海这件事变得不再那么重要，人们认为本地报界将以相应的冷淡态度对待这一问题，并停止刊登相关文章。

特务科副督察长的观点已传达给 KOMOR 先生，他对本处对其信件内容的处理方式表示满意。

Ja Pitts
D. S.

Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

Ever since German Emigrants have started arriving here, it has been our endeavour to prevent the Press from exploiting them for political propaganda or "news story" purposes.

Emigrants are instructed, on arrival here, NOT to give any interviews to the Press and to refrain from any political expressions or views and activities.

It is in the nature of things, that with such a mass of Emigrants any individual control is almost impossible but, I am glad to say, that instances of disregard of our instructions in the above connection have been few and even when such cases arose, it was mainly due to the efficiency of Press-reporters and news-story writers, that stories found their way into the local papers.

I must also say that the foreign language press, when approached, have shown appreciation of the reasons why we thought it undesirable that Emigrants stories should appear in their columns and I might state that these reasons are simply, that the Emigrants still are German subjects and under the protection of the German-Consulate General and, besides, they have friends and relatives at home to whose advantage it would certainly not be if Emigrant undertook political propaganda here directed against the Reich.

It has been our policy to tell all Emigrants, that what they left behind them in experiences, was no concern of ours and was best left alone, and that our sole concern was that, seeing that they were here, they got a fresh start as far as it was in our means to help them to that end.

Nevertheless, from time to time "interviews" do appear and I have been requested by the German Consulate General to give this matter earnest attention, when a case arises.

Thus, I am informed that the "Hwa Pao" Chinese paper brought, on the 13th inst. an interview by a doctor who related his experiences. Also that the "China Weekly Review" sometime ago (date not known) brought an article which the German authorities here consider to have been at least superfluous.

My intention in writing to you today is, to request you to please use your good influence with the Press in the sense, that all sensational stories be eliminated and interviews with Emigrants given no room in the papers.

尊敬的先生：

自从德国移民开始抵达这里以来，我们一直努力防止报界利用他们进行政治宣传或作为“新闻故事”的素材。

移民在抵达此处时被指示，不得接受报界采访，并避免任何政治言论、观点及活动。

鉴于移民数量庞大，对个人的控制在性质上几乎是不可能的，但我很高兴地说，违反上述指示的情况寥寥无几；即使出现此类情况，也主要是由于报社记者和新闻撰稿人的高效运作，使得这些故事得以见诸本地报端。

我还必须指出，外文报界在被接洽时，对我们认为不宜在其版面刊登移民故事的理由表示理解。我可以说明，这些理由很简单：移民仍然是德国臣民，受德国总领事馆的保护；此外，他们在国内有亲友，如果移民在这里从事针对德意志帝国（Reich）的政治宣传，显然对这些亲友不利。

我们的政策是告知所有移民，他们过去的经历与我们无关，最好置之不理；我们唯一关心的是，既然他们已来到这里，就在我们能力范围内帮助他们重新开始。

尽管如此，“采访”仍不时出现，德国总领事馆已要求我在案件发生时认真关注此事。

因此，我获悉中文报纸《华报》于本月13日刊登了一位医生讲述其经历的采访。此外，《密勒氏评论报》不久前（日期不详）刊登了一篇文章，此地德国当局认为该文章至少是多余的。

我今天致函阁下的意图，是恳请阁下运用您对报界的良好影响力，消除所有耸人听闻的故事，并不给刊登移民采访留出空间。

Hwa Pao published on June 13, 1939, the following article
written by one "Mou Hwa" ( 莫華 ):

The following is a statement made by a Jewish refugee
about the trying experiences, the insult and the ill-treatment
he had received on his way to Shanghai after his deportation
from Germany. His statement exposes the tyranny of the
Fascist nation:-

"I am a doctor by profession. and had practised as one
in Germany for more than 20 years. A policy of ill-treating
Jews was vigorously enforced in Germany, and we suffered
terribly though we have always been law-abiding.

"The anti-Jewish movement of the German Government
began in March or April last year. The first step taken was
to sever all economic connections with Jews. No persons were
allowed to make purchases from Jewish shops. This wicked
and poisonous policy had no satisfactory result, because the
Jewish shops were still crowded with clients. This state of
affairs lasted until after summer, and it was generally
believed that it would be allowed to continue. Unfortunately,
yet more wicked and poisonous methods were to follow.

"On September 19, all the Jews were ordered
by the Government to suspend operations and to leave the country
from that date. Any Jew who failed to comply with these
instructions after October 1 would be arrested and forcibly
deported.

"You all realize that we are all business men. All
our property was kept at the place where we lived. We of course
know that we were powerless so long as the German Government
was determined to exert this cruel pressure upon us, but where
were we to go in our penniless state?

"At the expiration of the period, many Jewish merchants
were arrested. False charges were brought against them and
they were forced to make confessions under torture. Heaven

《华报》于1939年6月13日发表了由一位名为“莫华”（Mou Hwa）的人撰写的以下文章：

以下是一位犹太难民关于其在被驱逐出德国后前往上海途中所经历的磨难、侮辱和虐待的陈述。他的陈述揭露了法西斯国家的暴政：-

“我是一名职业医生，并在德国行医超过20年。德国严厉执行迫害犹太人的政策，尽管我们一直守法，却遭受了可怕的苦难。

“德国政府的反犹运动始于去年三月或四月。采取的第一步是切断与犹太人的所有经济联系。任何人都不允许从犹太商店购物。这种邪恶且恶毒的政策并未取得令人满意的结果，因为犹太商店里依然顾客盈门。这种状况一直持续到夏季之后，人们普遍认为这种情况会被允许继续下去。不幸的是，随后出现了更邪恶、更恶毒的手段。

“9月19日，政府命令所有犹太人停止营业，并从即日起离开该国。任何在10月1日后未能遵守这些指令的犹太人将被逮捕并强制驱逐。

“你们都明白，我们都是商人。我们所有的财产都保留在我们居住的地方。当然，我们知道，只要德国政府决心对我们施加这种残酷的压力，我们就无能为力，但在身无分文的情况下，我们能去哪里呢？

“期限届满时，许多犹太商人被捕。他们被加上虚假的指控，并在酷刑下被迫认罪。天

knows that all the charges were false, but how were' we to
make complaints? Many Jews were thus sent to a concentration
camp where life was hundred times worse than in hell. For me,
I prefered death rather than to walk into the concentration

"As I know that there could be no hope to make a
living in Germany, I made up my mind to leave. I then took

"I shall never forget some of the tragic scenes .
You know that a number of Jews are married to German women.
The Jews are deported but their wives are allowed to remain
in Germany and as a result you can imagine some of the tragic
scenes. Some German women stood by their husbands in
happiness or suffering, but most of the Jews do not like to
see their beloved wives wandering about the world with them

the history of mankind. All the while the whips of the

Many pairs of sweethearts were thus parted forever amidst

"When I left Germany, I sent a letter by air mail to

I learned that my petition had not yet been settled. Owing to

知道所有指控都是捏造的，但我们如何申诉呢？许多犹太人因此被送往集中营，那里的生活比地狱还要糟糕百倍。对我而言，我宁愿死也不愿走进集中营。

“由于我知道在德国已无谋生希望，我决定离开。随后，我带上了一些必需品和法律允许带出境的金钱。我其余的所有财产均被没收。幸运的是，在上帝的帮助下，我没有遇到任何困难并抵达了上海。我在德国警察的押送下登船，途中受到严密监视。

“我永远不会忘记一些悲惨的场景。你们知道，许多犹太人与德国妇女结婚。犹太人被驱逐，但其妻子被允许留在德国，因此你可以想象一些悲惨的场景。一些德国妇女无论幸福还是痛苦都陪伴在她们的丈夫身边，但大多数犹太人不愿看到他们心爱的妻子随他们流浪世界并遭受苦难，所以他们抛弃了妻子和孩子。在码头告别时，撕裂空气的哭喊声将被载入人类历史上最悲惨的一页。与此同时，警察的鞭子像雨点一样无情地落在他们身上。许多对恋人就这样在哭喊和咒骂中永远分离。

“当我离开德国时，我曾通过航空邮件致信香港总督，请求允许我在香港行医，但当我途经香港时，得知我的申请尚未得到处理。由于停留时间短暂，我无法完成必要的程序。因此，我来到了上海。我将

"I feel greatly honoured at being able to come to
China. I know that only China is sympathetic towards the
homeless Jewish wanderer. In Shanghai we shall endeavour

China Weekly Review (10-6-39)
SHANGHAI RECEIVES MORE VICTIMS OF ANTI-SEMITISM; CUBA REJECTS 900

Shanghai's Jewish refugee population touched the 10,500 mark last Sunday when the Lloyd Triestino liner Conte Verde brought an additional 465 of these unfortunates here. The new arrivals were met by representatives of the local Refugee Committee and housed in the various camps which the committee has been instrumental in establishing during the past few months. By the end of this year, according to present indications, the local Jewish refugee population will be increased to fully 20,000.

The tragic fate of the Jews, fleeing from Nazi persecution in Germany, including the territories Nazified during the past year, was poignantly emphasized last week when more than 900 of these unfortunates were denied entry to Cuba after they had apparently received visas entitling them to enter the country.

Cuba Turns Them Down
They had shipped out from Germany in the Hamburg-America liner St. Louis and arrived at Havana on May 31. Approximately 100 were permitted to land out of a total of nearly 1,000. The Cuban authorities declared the papers of the remainder were not in order, and the St. Louis was obliged to return to Germany. One of the refugees, a man, slashed his wrist and jumped overboard in an effort to end his life. The ship's officers, fearing mass suicides, placed special guards over other refugees who were in a state of hysterical breakdown when they learned they were to be returned to Germany. Cuban police launches escorted the St. Louis outside the harbor limits to frustrate would-be suicides.

Well-Calculated Policy
An illuminating dissertation on the Jewish refugee problem and the wave of anti-Semitism which has arisen in Europe was contributed to the Mar. 18 issue of the Saturday Evening Post by Demaree Bess, European correspondent of the Christian Science Monitor. In the view of Mr. Bess, the current persecution of the Jews on the Old Continent cannot be understood as an emotional aberration. On the contrary, he contends, it has become a cold and deliberately-calculated policy of the totalitarian states designed to serve well-understood economic and political aims.

In the case of Germany, anti-Semitism has been a device for expropriating the properties of Jews and thereby easing the economic situation of the Third Reich. Fascist Italy, on the other hand, having proclaimed itself the champion of the cause of the Arabs against Britain and France, finds anti-Semitism a useful means of winning Arab sympathy, since Jews and Arabs are pitted against each other in Palestine where Britain, at least up to the recent publication of the White Paper, appeared in the role of protector of the Jews. By exploiting this Arab-Jewish antagonism, Mussolini aims to weaken both Britain and France in their Near Eastern possessions and throughout the Arab world generally.

Explaining the still cautious anti-Semitism of the Japanese Government—which appears especially incongruous in Japan, because there are practically no Jews in the country—Mr. Bess wrote:
"Thus far, the Japanese have made practical application of their new anti-Semitic code only in Eastern Europe. Being men of one-track minds, Japanese rulers are concentrating their full attention now upon strengthening their position in China. But Japanese leaders realized, sooner than some other statesmen, that the fate of Eastern Asia is closely related to events in Europe. The most formidable obstacle to Japanese control of China—aside from the Chinese themselves—is Soviet Russia. The Russians, in spite of their own internal difficulties, have managed to keep up an underground war against the Japanese forces in China, playing an active part in the Chinese guerrilla movement, which threatens even yet to wear down by slow degrees the Japanese conquerors.

《密勒氏评论报》（1939年6月10日）
上海接收更多反犹主义受害者；古巴拒绝900人

上周日，随着劳埃德·特里斯蒂诺轮船公司（Lloyd Triestino）的“康特·韦尔德”号（Conte Verde）班轮载着另外465名不幸者抵达此处，上海的犹太难民人数达到了10,500人的关口。新来者受到了当地难民委员会代表的迎接，并被安置在该委员会过去几个月里协助建立的各个难民营中。根据目前的迹象，到今年年底，当地的犹太难民人口将增至整整20,000人。

上周，当900多名显然已获得入境签证的不幸者在古巴被拒绝入境时，那些逃离德国（包括过去一年中被纳粹化的地区）纳粹迫害的犹太人的悲惨命运得到了令人痛心的强调。

古巴拒绝他们入境
他们乘坐汉堡-美洲轮船公司（Hamburg-America）的“圣路易斯”号（St. Louis）班轮从德国出发，于5月31日抵达哈瓦那。在近1,000人的总数中，约有100人被允许上岸。古巴当局宣布其余人员的证件不符合规定，“圣路易斯”号被迫返回德国。一名男性难民割腕并跳海，试图结束自己的生命。船上的官员担心发生集体自杀事件，对其他得知将被遣返德国而处于歇斯底里崩溃状态的难民加强了看守。古巴警方的巡逻艇护送“圣路易斯”号驶出港口界限，以阻止企图自杀者。

精心算计的政策
《基督教科学箴言报》驻欧洲记者德马里·贝斯（Demaree Bess）在3月18日出版的《星期六晚邮报》上发表了一篇关于犹太难民问题及欧洲兴起的反犹主义浪潮的发人深省的文章。在贝斯先生看来，旧大陆当前对犹太人的迫害不能被理解为一种情绪失常。相反，他认为，这已成为极权国家为实现众所周知的经济和政治目标而采取的一种冷酷且经过深思熟虑的政策。

就德国而言，反犹主义是一种没收犹太人财产的手段，从而缓解第三帝国的经济状况。另一方面，法西斯意大利自称是阿拉伯人对抗英国和法国事业的捍卫者，发现反犹主义是赢得阿拉伯人同情的有用手段，因为在巴勒斯坦，犹太人和阿拉伯人相互对立，而英国至少在最近发表白皮书之前，似乎扮演着犹太人保护者的角色。通过利用这种阿拉伯-犹太人的敌对关系，墨索里尼旨在削弱英国和法国在其近东属地以及整个阿拉伯世界的影响力。

在解释日本政府仍然谨慎的反犹主义时——这在日本显得尤其不协调，因为该国实际上没有犹太人——贝斯先生写道：
“到目前为止，日本人仅在东欧实际应用了他们新的反犹法典。日本统治者是一群思维单一的人，目前正全神贯注于加强其在中国的地位。但日本领导人比某些其他政治家更早意识到，东亚的命运与欧洲的事件密切相关。除了中国人本身之外，日本控制中国的最可怕障碍是苏维埃俄国。尽管俄罗斯人自身面临内部困难，但他们设法在中国对日军保持着一场地下战争，积极参与中国游击运动，这场运动甚至至今仍有可能逐渐消耗日本征服者。

along the borders of Manchuria, Outer Mongolia and Korea. And
Japanese agents also are active in European countries along
Russia's western borders. They are doing what can be done to
encourage movements designed to break up European Russia, including
the movement for an independent Ukraine. And anti-Semitism is
a convenient instrument for stirring up anti-Soviet feeling in
most of the countries of eastern Europe....I lived and worked

page_data.en:
China Weekly Review(4-2-39)
JEWISH REFUGEES SHOULD BE WELCOMED AND ASSISTED HERE!

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, the sole American daily in the local afternoon field, distinguished itself ignobly on Monday of this week by raising a cry for the closure of Shanghai to future would-be Jewish emigrants fleeing from the bestial fury of the fascist persecutors of their race in Europe.
"Somehow it is going to be necessary to stop this influx," the paper said in a leading editorial, recommending an immediate session of the Consular Body to deal with the "alarmingly growing problem." The Post thus ranged itself alongside all those who express humanitarian sentiments where the Jews are concerned, but balk at giving practical aid - if that aid shows signs of costing them something.
The Post said there was something "almost terrifying" in the news that an additional 1,000 Jewish refugees will arrive here shortly on the Conte Biancamano. It does not seem to have occurred to the Post that it is much more terrifying to be a victim of Nazi hate and to have no place to which to escape, to know of no country willing to do more than express-like the Post-pious words of sympathy.
Since our contemporary is apparently concerned about a possible public expense angle of the local refugee problem, let it be pointed out that the recent Jewish arrivals in Shanghai have been taken care of, for the most part, by Jewish organizations and individuals, with such additional aid as could be garnered from other sources. Relief organizations abroad have helped, too. The refugees have cost our municipal treasuries exactly nothing. Why, then, the almost hysterical alarm?
Shanghai is one of the few spots on earth to which pitiful victims of Europe's totalitarian terror can still emigrate freely. The Post wants to close this last remaining door.
If Shanghai were threatened with an influx of forty or fifty thousand refugees from Germany and Austria there might be ground for apprehension, but the 1,200 who have arrived and the 1,000 who are allegedly enroute, will not cause any special complications. Surely a municipality which has been able to weather one of the most notorious "salary grab" scandals ever staged anywhere, should be able to handle the problem of temporarily providing support for a few hundred, or even a few thousand refugees from Nazi terrorism.. But, as stated in the foregoing, neither the International Settlement nor the French Concession has spent a dollar yet-on the care of Jewish refugees. Also, neither settlement has strained itself financially to care for the millions of Chinese refugees who were driven into the foreign-administered areas by Japanese frightfulness. The support of these millions of unfortunate Chinese has been shouldered entirely by charitably inclined people in America and Britain, and by the Chinese people here and their government in Chungking. The authorities of the International Settlement haven't even had sufficient energy or humanitarian instinct to provide a "flop-house" for homeless people to sleep in at night-instead of on the sidewalks-in this winter weather.
We, obviously, have no desire to direct this subject into mercenary channels, but it is a fact-which strangely enough has not occurred to the Post. - that the Shanghai foreign Settlements owe much of their prosperity to refugees. Shortly after the establishment of the Settlements in the middle of the past century, the Taiping Rebellion broke out and drove thousands of Chinese refugees into the foreign areas, thus providing, almost overnight, the dense populations which made these areas a paradise for real estate speculators. This situation, characterized by further influxes of Chinese refugees, was repeated at the time of the Boxer Rebellion in 1900, and again at the time of the first revolution in 1911, and after that the political disturbances were almost continuous through the era of the warlords from 1911 to 1927, and each one drove Chinese refugees into the foreign Settlements with consequent increases in real estate values and rentals of property. Then along about 1917 the Russian revolution sent more refugees here-white men this time-and again Shanghai benefitted. Charitably-inclined foreigners and Chinese maintained soup-kitchens for a time but it was not many
page_data.zh:
《密勒氏评论报》（1939年2月4日）
应欢迎并援助来沪的犹太难民！

作为本地下午时段唯一的美国日报，《上海晚邮报与水星报》（The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury）在本周一表现卑劣，它呼吁对将来为逃避欧洲法西斯种族迫害者的兽性狂怒而试图移民的犹太人关闭上海大门。
“无论如何，必须阻止这股涌入，”该报在一篇社论中说道，建议领事团立即召开会议以处理这一“惊人增长的问题”。《晚邮报》 thus 将自己与那些在涉及犹太人问题时表达人道主义情感、但在援助显示出要让他们付出代价时就退缩的人归为一类。
《晚邮报》称，另有1,000名犹太难民即将乘坐“康特·比安卡马诺”号（Conte Biancamano）抵达此处的消息有些“几乎令人恐惧”。《晚邮报》似乎没有想到，成为纳粹仇恨的受害者且无处可逃，知道没有任何国家愿意做得比像《晚邮报》那样表达虔诚的同情言辞更多，这才是更加令人恐惧的。
既然我们的同行显然担心本地难民问题可能涉及的公共开支角度，需要指出的是，最近抵达上海的犹太难民主要由犹太组织和个人照顾，辅之以从其他来源筹集的额外援助。国外的救济组织也提供了帮助。难民们未让我们的市政财政花费分文。那么，为何会有近乎歇斯底里的恐慌？
上海是地球上少数几个欧洲极权恐怖主义的可怜受害者仍能自由移民的地方之一。《晚邮报》想要关上这扇仅存的大门。
如果上海面临来自德国和奥地利的四五万难民的涌入威胁，或许确有担忧的理由，但已抵达的1,200人和据称在途中的1,000人不会引起任何特殊的复杂情况。毫无疑问，一个能够经受住有史以来最臭名昭著的“薪俸贪污”丑闻之一的市政当局，应该有能力处理暂时为数以百计甚至数千名来自纳粹恐怖主义的难民提供支持的问题。但是，如前所述，国际公共租界和法租界尚未在照顾犹太难民方面花费一美元。同样，两个租界也未在财政上竭尽全力去照顾因日本人的暴行而被驱入外人管理区域的数百万中国难民。对这些数百万不幸中国人的支持完全由美国和英国具有慈善倾向的人士、这里的中国人民及其在重庆的政府承担。国际公共租界的当局甚至没有足够的精力或人道主义本能，在这个冬季天气里，为无家可归者提供一个夜间睡觉的“廉价寄宿处”，而不是让他们睡在人行道上。
显然，我们无意将此话题引向唯利是图的渠道，但有一个事实——奇怪的是《晚邮报》并未想到——即上海外人租界的繁荣在很大程度上归功于难民。在上个世纪中叶租界建立后不久，太平天国运动爆发，将成千上万的中国难民驱入外人区域，从而几乎在一夜之间提供了密集的人口，使这些区域成为房地产投机者的天堂。这种情况随着中国难民的进一步涌入，在1900年义和团运动时期重演，随后在1911年第一次革命时期再次重演，此后从1911年到1927年的军阀混战时代政治动荡几乎持续不断，每一次都将中国难民驱入外人租界，随之而来的是房地产价值和租金的增加。然后在1917年左右，俄国革命送来了更多的难民——这次是白人——上海再次受益。具有慈善倾向的外国人和中国人维持了一段时间的施粥所，但没过几个月

page_data.en:
2
months before the Russians had dug in and found a new home for
themselves here-contributing again to the prosperity and well-
being of the city-particularly the French Concession, the chief
street of which-Avenue Joffre-resembled a cow-path before the Russians
developed it into a first-class retail center.
And now, the Jewish refugees from Germany (rather Austria)
arrive, and Shanghai again will-or should -benefit in even greater
measure than has been the case in the past, because these refugees
do not come from the lower peasant strata, but from the trained and
cultural middle and upper-middle classes. Most of them, if
treated properly, should be able to establish a foothold in a com-
paratively short time. If handled intelligently, this new element
in the population might be of greatest value in offsetting the
demoralizing influence of the Japanese invasion.. It is questionable
whether the Consular Body has any power to interfere with the
landing of Jewish refugees at this port, even though the consular
officials might wish to do so. A more sensible and humanitarian
suggestion would be for the Consular Body to advise the authorities
of the Settlements to bestir themselves and help the unfortunate
refugees to establish themselves here.
page_data.zh:
2
俄罗斯人就在此扎根并找到了新家——再次为城市的繁荣和福祉做出了贡献——尤其是法租界，其主要街道霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）在俄罗斯人将其发展为一流零售中心之前，看起来就像一条牛径。
现在，来自德国（更确切地说是奥地利）的犹太难民抵达，上海将——或者应该——比以往任何时候都更多地受益，因为这些难民并非来自下层农民阶层，而是来自受过训练和有文化的中等及中上层阶级。如果得到妥善对待，他们中的大多数人应该能够在相对较短的时间内站稳脚跟。如果处理得当，人口中的这一新元素可能在抵消日本入侵造成的士气低落影响方面具有最大价值。即使领事官员希望这样做，领事团是否有权力干涉犹太难民在本港登陆也是值得怀疑的。一个更明智且更具人道主义精神的建议是，领事团建议租界当局行动起来，帮助这些不幸的难民在此安家落户。

MAINICHI 7·6·39

NEW FACTORY TO BE ESTABLISHED FOR REFUGEE JEWS

Nine thousand Jews have already
arrived in Shanghai and two thousand more are expected
in autumn. Some of them have some means to earn a
livelihood independently, but the majority are poor.
It is said that a factory will
be established to give employment to Jews. The authorities
of the International Settlement and the French Concession
are studying ways and means to assist them. The Consular
Body is reported to be considering support for Jews. It is
believed that a new factory will be established in the
near future.

《每日新闻》 1939年6月7日

将为犹太难民建立新工厂

已有九千名犹太人抵达上海，预计秋季还将有两千人抵达。他们中有些人有独立谋生的手段，但大多数人是穷人。
据说将建立一家工厂以提供就业机会给犹太人。国际公共租界和法租界的当局正在研究协助他们的方法和途径。据报道，领事团正在考虑对犹太人的支持。相信不久的将来将建立一家新工厂。

K 38/1

THE INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE FOR THE ORGANIZATION OF EUROPEAN
IMMIGRANTS IN CHINA

Shanghai, January 17, 1941.

Shanghai Municipal Council,
Revenue Department,
Shanghai.

Dear Sirs,

I beg to hand you herewith statistical
figures which I believe will prove of interest to you.
We have gone to great pains in ascertaining from our
Card-Index the distribution of residents as shown in
the statement, but I would observe that owing to the
frequent and rapid changes of addresses, it will not
be possible in the future to arrive at exact figures
as to the proportion of Refugees living in the three
districts enumerated.

So long as there is no new important
influx of Refugees, this proportion may be accepted
as permanent because, whilst one party may move from
the French Concession to Hongkew, another party at
the same time moves from Hongkew to the French Con-
cession so that actually the fluctuation of residents
cannot show very great discrepancies.

All the same, I would observe that the
figures shown cannot lay claim to absolute accuracy
because registration not being compulsory nor yet the
notification of changes of address, necessarily there
might be some inexactitude in our records.

Trusting that this report will prove
useful, I beg to remain, dear Sirs,

Yours faithfully,

(Sd) P. Komor

Hon. Secretary.

只要没有新的大规模难民涌入，这一比例可被视为固定不变，因为虽然一部分人可能从法租界搬至虹口，但与此同时另一部分人从虹口搬至法租界，因此实际上居民的流动不会显示出很大的差异。

尽管如此，我必须指出，所示数字不能声称具有绝对准确性，因为登记并非强制性的，地址变更的通知也非强制性，因此我们的记录中必然存在一些不确切之处。

相信本报告将证明有用，谨此致意，尊敬的先生们，

您忠实的，

(签名) P. Komor

Date November 11, 1933.

Subject (in full) Germans of the Jewish faith who have recently arrived in
Shanghai.

Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by [Signature] D.I.

With reference to the endorsement of the Officer i/c
Special Branch appearing on the attached translation from
"Journal de Shanghai" dated November 7, 1933, I have to
report that two batches of Germans of the Jewish faith
have arrived in Shanghai recently. The majority of these
persons are physicians or surgeons who have come here with
the object of escaping from what they term the "harsh" regime
at present existent in Germany, and to set up practices in
some of the larger towns in China. Without exception
these gentlemen all appear to be fairly well off financially
and some of them hope to commence business in the near
future.

It has been learned that a further draft of German
physicians of the Jewish faith contemplate proceeding to
China, but the local German Consulate-General authorities
have cabled Berlin that it would be unwise for any further
Jewish practitioners to come here since there are too many
doctors of all nationalities striving to make a living at
present.

The following is a list giving some details of the
newly arrived German doctors, etc. of the Jewish faith:

- ex s.s. "Conte Rosso" - October 2, 1933 -

✓ Max DAHLE, aged 32, physician, travels on German Pass-
port No. 263/30 issued by the Police at
Zudenscheid on July 29, 1930, and which
bears the visa of the Chinese Consulate-
General at Berlin dated August 4, 1933.
Is accompanied by his wife Gerda DAHLE,
aged 23.

鉴于附上的1933年11月7日《上海日报》（Journal de Shanghai）译文中特别处负责人的批注，本人谨此报告，近期有两批犹太裔德国人抵达上海。这些人中大多数是医生或外科医师，他们来此的目的是为了逃离目前存在于德国的所谓“严酷”政权，并在中国的一些较大城镇开设诊所。这些先生们无一例外地似乎都拥有相当不错的经济状况，其中一些人希望在不久的将来开始营业。

据悉，另一批犹太裔德国医生正计划前往中国，但当地德国总领事馆当局已致电柏林称，鉴于目前各国籍医生都在努力谋生，人数过多，再有犹太从业者前来是不明智的。
